title: Launch Budget Coordinator, STR Property Launches (Reconciliation Heavy, US Hours)
job_title: Launch Budget Coordinator, STR Property Launches (Reconciliation Heavy, US Hours)
description: LAUNCH BUDGET COORDINATOR, SHORT-TERM RENTAL PROPERTY LAUNCHES Remote. US business hours. PLEASE READ THIS WHOLE POST BEFORE APPLYING. There are instructions at the bottom, and how you follow them is the first thing we look at. ABOUT US We run full-service, hands-off management for short-term rental owners across the US. Part of that is launching a property: an owner hands us an empty house and we furnish it, wire it, stock it, style it, photograph it and open it to guests. The owner pays one all-in launch budget for that. Furniture, tech, accessories, and the services that install them. This seat owns the record of every dollar in that budget. It is reconciliation work: vendor invoices against what we committed to, card charges against the plan, receipts filed the day they exist, spreadsheets that have to tie. We automate everything software can do. What software cannot do is notice that a vendor invoice and a card statement disagree by $16.48, d ---------- that the $16.48 matters, and go find out why. Right now that work sits with our founder, and that is the whole reason this seat exists. We are growing, this is the first seat of its kind here, and it will not be the last one. WHAT THIS ROLE REALLY IS Every case below is real. The amounts are changed, for the same reason we explain further down. Nineteen furniture lines on a live property are flagged as ordered. There is no order number behind any of them, no charge on any card, and no confirmation from the vendor. Either they were bought and nobody wrote it down, or somebody typed a word into the wrong cell. The difference is $4,318.62. If you place that order and it was already placed, the owner pays for the same furniture twice, and nobody finds out for a month. That is the job. Here is more of it, in the same week. - Two lines carry the same item name and two different product links, so the house is getting either four sofas or two, a $2,144.75 question, and the owner is reading it as one line. - A vendor invoice hit the card as $9,340.55 on one day and another $812.07 a week later, because that vendor captures payment as items ship. The record held only the first number, so the property looked $812.07 cheaper than it was. - A tax column on a delivery showed $22.50 per mattress and nothing on the other sixty items. That is not tax. It is a state recycling fee that is legitimately owed, and two people here have already gotten it wrong. - A four-figure order shipped to one property's address and belonged to a different property's plan. The ship-to address is never the answer. The item list is. - One plan column read $10,462.31 against an order total of $10,462.08. A twenty-three cent gap between two numbers computed from completely different inputs made the row look reconciled while the real figure underneath it sat $1,384.90 low. Every one of those is solvable. None of them is solvable by someone who is willing to let it go. So the honest description of this role: it is detective work on money. Most days it is a spreadsheet, a vendor invoice, a receipt and a browser. It is quiet and it is deliberate. The person who is great at it is the person who genuinely cannot leave a number alone when it does not tie, who would rather spend forty minutes finding the missing $16.48 than type over the cell and move on, and who gets a small amount of satisfaction when the last line finally closes at zero. Your job in one sentence: keep the record true enough that the close-out number is right the first time. By the time that number goes to an owner there is very little left for anyone to check, because you kept the record true for the three months leading up to it. We read it before it goes anywhere, and it goes out over our name, not yours. This is not task-based VA work. Nobody is going to send you a list each morning telling you which rows to price or which invoice to open. You run a weekly rhythm and you can read your own dashboard, so you already know. If that reads as tedious to you, we would genuinely rather you skip this one. If it reads as a puzzle, keep going. WHAT YOU WILL OWN Your instrument is one Google Sheet per property, our launch budget tracker. It is the single record of what the property is buying, what it committed to, what actually got charged, and what is left. Every property in flight has one and you run all of them. You grow into this in two phases. Phase one is keeping the record true on properties that are already running. Phase two is owning a property's budget from the day the tracker opens to the day it closes. PHASE ONE, KEEPING THE RECORD TRUE - Price every row on the plan that has no price. Find the item, confirm the variant, the size and the pack quantity, and put a real number on it. - Load the Amazon and Wayfair carts against the plan. This is more mechanical than it sounds and it has real traps. Our Amazon cart holds a hard 50 lines, and line 51 silently pushes the oldest line out into Saved for later, so a 152 row accessories list is four separate orders and you d ---------- the batches up front. Re-adding an item that is already in the cart raises its quantity instead of warning you. You verify by item code and quantity, never by the badge in the corner. - Tag every order back onto the plan rows it paid for, so nothing is bought that the sheet does not know about. - Log every card charge as its own row, with the invoice's true order total rather than the first posting that showed up, and file the receipt the day it exists. A charge with no receipt cannot be cleanly billed back, which means a missing receipt is money the company cannot recover that month. - Reconcile every vendor invoice against what we actually committed to, line by line, and produce the defect list. What was charged, what was ordered, what is missing, what does not agree, and which of those is a real problem versus a coi ---------- . - Run the flag pass every Friday. Filter the exception column and clear everything that is not clean. Some of our checks run from scripts on our side and we run them against your sheet, so your pass has to be clean before it reaches them. - Chase our designer for the receipts, the property attributions and the open answers that nobody else is going to chase. The buying happens in person, in other states, on a company card, and store receipts print department codes instead of product names, so only the person who was standing there can say which room a $340 receipt belongs to. Nobody else will chase that, and after you start, nobody else has to. This is the one genuinely persistent, human thread in the job and it is a large part of its value. PHASE TWO, OWNING THE BUDGET END TO END - Open a tracker for a new property from our template and type the house into the quantity calculator: bedrooms, beds by size, baths, sleeps, TVs, floors. Half the quantities in the plan calculate themselves off those numbers, so this is not data entry, it is the foundation. Every count comes from a written source, and when two written sources disagree you flag it instead of picking a winner. - Take the designer's spec in when it changes and surface what it moved: what got more expensive, what got cheaper, and which rows quietly disappeared. Never hand-merge two lists. - Watch the envelope. The plan has a cap, and the week you first see that the plan is going to cross it, you say so out loud. Weeks early, not at the end. Warning early is the entire point of the number. - Compute what owner money may be sent to pay down the company card, name the specific charges it covers, and evidence every one with a receipt. Then record the settlement against every row it paid. A row you forget to mark as settled asks for the same money again next month. - Produce the close-out: the reconciliation that says whether the owner is owed a refund or owes a true-up, and the drafted invoice or refund figure behind it. HELPING BUILD THE SYSTEM - We have a written playbook for this seat and we are still finishing the SOPs behind it. You will help write them, in your own words, out of the work you actually did. - Write down why a sheet looks the way it does, so the next person does not have to re-derive it. As we add properties this becomes more than one seat, and the person who runs it well is the person who trains the next one. WHAT YOU WILL NOT DO, AND THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT SECTION IN THIS POST You own the record. You never own the movement. Nothing you do debits a bank, releases a wire, pays a card, or reaches an owner's inbox. Not once, not in an emergency, not on a deadline. - You never fire a charge. Every single payment, card or eCheck or wire, is approved personally by our founder, on that specific charge, every time. There is no batch approval and there is no standing permission. - You never move money out of any bank or merchant account. You compute what should be paid and you evidence it. He releases it. - You do not place the orders. You build the cart, you verify it line by line, you hand it over with the batch, the total, the shipping address and the property reference it needs, and somebody else presses the button. - You are not the property owner's contact. Not the approval schedule, not an invoice, not a refund figure, not an email with a number in it. You draft. We send. Always. - You never add, edit or verify a vendor's bank details or payee information. Nobody in this seat does. That is the wall against invoice fraud, and urgency is the exact pretext it exists to defeat. - You have no banking, no payment gateway and no accounting system access, on purpose. If you ever find that you somehow can reach one, you do not act, you report it. Read that as protection, not as distrust. The seat that keeps the record of the money is deliberately not the seat that moves it, because a record that can move money is not a record, it is an opinion. That separation is what makes your close-out number worth something, and it means that when money goes somewhere it should not have, it is structurally impossible for it to have been you. Very few jobs this close to real dollars give you that. We designed it that way on purpose, we will not ask you to bend it, and we think it is one of the best parts of the offer. A WORD ABOUT CONFIDENTIALITY You will see what we pay for goods and what the owner is billed for them. That information does not leave the company, ever, for any reason, including to an owner who asks you directly and including when they are being nice about it. If that is not a line you can hold comfortably, please do not apply. It is written into the agreement and we take it seriously. The same applies in the other direction. You never structure anything: no splitting an order, sequencing a purchase, or shaping a number so it sits under a threshold. And no order, vendor or reimbursement that benefits you or anyone connected to you. Either one is immediate cause, even if the underlying purchase was perfectly fine. We say it out loud so nobody is surprised by it later. MUST-HAVES We are not going to write detail oriented here, because everybody says it about themselves and it predicts nothing. Here is what actually predicts success in this seat. - 2+ years in a role where reconciling one document against another was the actual job. Accounts payable, bookkeeping, procurement, ecommerce operations, inventory control, order desk, audit support. Something where a number had to tie and you were the one who made it tie. - You know that a total matching is not proof it is right. Two numbers built from completely different inputs can land within a dollar of each other by coi ---------- , look tied, and hide a four-figure error underneath. Somebody who checks totals and stops will not survive here. - You understand that one number can arrive as several charges. A single vendor order can hit a card as three postings weeks apart. Log the first one and the record is quietly wrong forever, and nothing on the sheet will tell you. - You chase small discrepancies to the bottom. If a total is off by $16.48, we need the person who finds the $16.48, not the person who adjusts the total. You are also the person who can chase it, find that it is a legitimate fee and not an error, and say so, instead of forcing it to tie. - You can hold an open discrepancy without doing either wrong thing with it. The two failure modes are dropping it because it is small and inventing a reason for it because you want it closed. Both are worse than a note that says unexplained, $16.48, chasing. If you have ever kept a variance open for two weeks because you refused to guess, tell us about it. - You leave alone what you do not understand. Some of our sheets carry hand-marked rows whose meaning was never written down. Our standing rule is preserve, never interpret. A near-pattern is a trap, not a shortcut, and finishing one makes six edits nobody can undo. If your instinct is to tidy first and ask later, this seat will hurt. - Real spreadsheet fluency, not proficient in Excel on a resume. SUMIFS, lookups, filters, spotting a hardcoded number sitting where a formula should be, and knowing what happens to a sheet when someone inserts a column into the middle of it. You will inherit sheets you did not build. We will test this and it is not a hard test if this is true of you. You do not need to code. - You can tell someone senior to you that a number is wrong. Comfortably, in writing, with the evidence attached, and without softening it into something they can miss. - You follow up politely and repeatedly with somebody who is busy and is not your subordinate. The designer chase is real and it does not resolve itself. - Stamina for a long pass. Some days are 150 rows of the same check. We need the 150th to get the same attention as the first. - Honest. If you have not confirmed something, you say so. You never report a status you did not verify and you never invent a number, a price, a quantity, a receipt or which property a charge belongs to. I do not know yet, here is how I am finding out, is always the right answer. This is the single most important item on this list and it is a hard gate at every stage of our process. - Clear, professional written English. You will write to a US designer and to US vendor support about money, and you will write notes somebody reads six months later to understand why a row looks the way it does. - Stable power and internet, plus a backup for outages. - Able to work the fixed shift below. Please read the hours section carefully before you apply. NICE-TO-HAVES - Amazon Business, Wayfair Professional, or any trade, wholesale or B2B purchasing account. - You have reconciled a credit card statement against a set of vendor invoices and found something. - You have chased a vendor for a credit and won. - Bookkeeping exposure, QuickBooks or Xero or similar, even read-only. You will not have a QuickBooks seat, but knowing what a reimbursement invoice has to say is useful. - Furniture, interior design, hospitality FF and E, or construction procurement background. - Short-term rental or property management background. - You have built a tracker or a process that somebody else then used without you in the room. - A little Google Apps Script or Python, or genuine curiosity about the scripts behind our sheets. Not required. Rewarded. HOURS AND TIMEZONE This is a fixed US business-hours shift. Please read this section before you d ---------- anything else about the job. - 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM US Pacific, Monday through Friday. Eight hours a day, 40 hours a week. - In the Philippines that is 12:00 AM to 8:00 AM the following day. Midnight to eight in the morning. That is an overnight shift and we are not going to describe it as anything else. - The shift moves by one hour when the US changes to and from daylight saving time. Nothing else changes. - The work itself is asynchronous in nature. Spreadsheets, invoices, receipts, carts, reconciliation. Almost none of it needs somebody else awake at the same moment, and you are not on a phone all day. The genuinely synchronous part is small: the designer, and occasionally a vendor's support line. Both of those sit inside the shift. - Our other US-facing seats run a ten hour US day. This one is eight. - You are online and responsive for the whole shift, not signed in with notifications off. - Some deadlines in this job are actual dates. The Friday flag pass happens on Friday. Ordering deadlines ahead of a launch are the other kind, and they do not move. - No weekends. Nothing lands on you outside the shift. Emergencies stay with us. Be honest with yourself about that before you apply. If midnight to 8:00 AM does not fit your life, please do not apply, and there is no hard feeling in that. If you are somewhere other than the Philippines, do the conversion yourself and tell us on the form what 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM Pacific is where you are. We do read that answer. COMPENSATION - $750 per month, for the arrangement above. - The rate is flat. Phase two pays the same as phase one. We would rather say that plainly than describe a step-up we have not committed to, so you can plan on this number. - Merit review at 90 days after conversion, then annually. That is where the rate gets revisited. - We honor 13th month pay. We offer flexible coordinated time off and we cover your equipment. We treat our people well and the good ones grow with us. - Paid trial first. Before any ongoing offer there is a short paid project, a couple of hours of real work, and we pay you for it. - The first four weeks are an Initial Evaluation Term at close to full rate, so both sides get a real look before anyone commits. HOW WE HIRE We use a multi-step process and it is deliberately demanding. Every stage is something you do on your own time, and we do not schedule a single call until you have already shown us how you work. In order: a short application form, a 2-minute video, a written reconciliation exercise, a personality assessment, then an interview and a paid trial. Budget roughly two to three hours of your own time across all of it before the paid trial, which we pay for. The personality assessment is a tiebreaker, not a gate, and nobody is rejected on it alone. Each step starts when you finish the one before it. There is no cohort and there is no closing date. The video request reaches you within a minute of your form landing, and you get 48 hours from that email. Clear it and the reconciliation exercise comes to you, with 72 hours from that email. Clear that and the assessment comes, with 24 hours. Every clock runs from your own email, not from a date on a calendar, so applying today and applying in a month get you exactly the same runway. This posting stays up until somebody accepts an offer. Then it comes down and the form closes. The reconciliation exercise is the stage that d ---------- this seat. It is a real invoice against a real plan with the names taken out, it does not tie, and the reason it does not tie is not the reason you will first think it is. There is no trick, but there is a wrong answer that most people give, and it is the confident one. Deadlines are real at every stage, and they are personal to you rather than to a calendar. If you miss one, you are out. Please do not ask for an extension. HOW TO APPLY Fill out the form linked at the very bottom of this post. Applications sent any other way will not be reviewed. Please do not message us on this platform, do not email us, and do not send a resume in a reply. Only form submissions are looked at. We know that is strict. It is the first filter and it is working as intended. Read the form carefully. One of the questions is there to check that you read this post. Apply here: ----------

description: Moscoso Express is a 20+ year trucking company in the United States specializing in expedited and air freight. We move time-sensitive shipments across the Midwest, and this role is where those shipments get planned. We are hiring Operations Support Specialists who already know freight. This is not an entry-level tracking or customer service role. You will plan and route orders, choose equipment, set appointments, and manage exceptions for a fleet that runs 24 hours a day. Please read the requirements carefully. We ask for a video and for details of your freight background and education, and we do not review applications that leave any of them out. What you will do: - Plan and route incoming orders: pickup and delivery windows, transit time, driver hours, and equipment (dry van, straight truck, sprinter, team vs solo) - D ---------- how each load runs: drop trailer or live load, appointment type, and sequencing when several orders overlap - Work across multiple US time zones at once and convert between them accurately - Coordinate with drivers, customers, and internal team members by phone and in writing - Monitor loads and give status updates before they are asked for - Resolve delays, weather, breakdowns, schedule changes, and pickup or delivery exceptions, and escalate with a clear summary and a recommended next step - Keep order records, shipment updates, and communications accurate and current - Work across a TMS, GPS tracking, spreadsheets, email, Slack, and customer portals Freight experience is required: This is the first thing we look at, so we want to be clear about it up front. We are looking for people who have worked in trucking or freight forwarding and have hands-on experience with several of the following: carriers and drivers, load planning or dispatch, FTL and LTL, a TMS (McLeod, Aljex, Ascend, Priority1, or similar), load boards (DAT, Truckstop), BOL, POD, and rate confirmations, track and trace, or forwarding operations. If your background is customer service, general virtual assistant work, ecommerce order tracking, warehouse-only, or BPO without freight, this role will not be the right fit, even if a past job title included "dispatch" or "logistics". We mention this so you can spend your time on roles that match your experience. Education: Freight planning is problem-solving with numbers, time, and distance, so we look for candidates whose studies built those skills. Engineering (industrial, mechanical, civil, or similar), logistics, supply chain management, transportation, or another science, technology, or math field is a strong match. Please tell us your degree or course and your school in your application. What we have learned about this role: We have trained several people in this role, and the ones who did well shared a few habits. We share them here so you can d ---------- whether this sounds like you. - You like to drive your own work. You start the next order, look ahead, and bring questions early rather than waiting to be told what to do next. - You read carefully. Our instructions are written, detailed, and in English, and you are comfortable reading them fully and applying them on your own. - You take feedback on board. When we adjust something, the next order shows the change. - You keep a good pace. A fully planned order should take about 15 to 20 minutes, and you will often plan several at once. Speed and accuracy both matter. - You speak up. If you are blocked, confused, or behind, you say so in Slack right away. We would much rather hear about a problem early than find it later. - You can explain your thinking. You can write a short, clear summary of what you did on an order and why you chose that plan. Working hours: Training runs on a fixed schedule in US Central Time, which we will confirm with you before you start. Your regular schedule is assigned during training. - Initial training: 2 weeks, Monday to Friday, on a fixed daily schedule in US Central Time. Please only apply if you can commit to all 10 training days. - Ongoing coaching continues through your first 3 months, alongside your regular shift. - After initial training: we operate 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, so regular schedules vary and may include weekend hours. Your shift is set with you during training. - All schedules are set in US Central Time, so your Philippine local hours and days will not match ours. A US daytime shift falls overnight in the Philippines, and a US evening shift falls during Philippine daytime. Philippine times shift one hour later when US daylight saving time ends in November. Working arrangement and pay: - The rate for this role is $9 - $11 USD per hour, based on your experience. At 40 hours per week, that is about $1,560 - $1,900 USD per month. - This is an independent contractor position, not employment. You are responsible for your own taxes and government contributions in the Philippines. - Training is also a trial period, for you as much as for us. It is a chance for both sides to see whether the role and the schedule are a good fit. During this period we are not able to promise work for any set length of time, and either side may d ---------- at any point that it is not the right match. We will be straightforward with you about how things are going, and we hope you will be just as open with us. If it is working well, we would very much like you to stay with us long term. - Pay is sent twice a month. - We use TimeProof for time tracking. You install the free TimeProof app from OnlineJobs.ph and sign in with your OnlineJobs.ph account. It records your working time and takes periodic screenshots of your screen while you are on shift. Your pay is based on this record. Please only apply if you are comfortable with screenshot-based time tracking. Home office requirements (required, and checked during training): - Two monitors or more. One screen is not workable for this role. - A headset with a microphone for calls with drivers and customers - Stable, fast internet and reliable power. A backup internet option is not required but is preferred. - A quiet workspace and a computer that runs several browser tabs, a TMS, and Slack at once without slowing down How to apply: Your application must include all three parts. Applications missing any of them are not reviewed. 1. A 1-2 minute video, in English, introducing yourself and describing one specific load or shipment you planned or handled: what the freight was, what decisions you made, and what went right or wrong. Use any of these: - Loom ( ---------- ) - free, records you and your screen in the browser, gives you a link instantly - YouTube - upload and set the video to "Unlisted" - Google Drive - upload and set sharing to "Anyone with the link" Open your link in a private/incognito window first to confirm it plays for someone outside your account. 2. Your freight background: the companies, your role, how long, and which of the systems and tasks above you used. 3. Your education: degree or course, and school. We look forward to hearing from you.

title: Performance Video Editor & Creative Strategist — AI-Driven DTC Health Ads ($1,000/mo+)
job_title: Performance Video Editor & Creative Strategist — AI-Driven DTC Health Ads ($1,000/mo+)
description: JOB OVERVIEW We are a fast-growing DTC health supplement brand (Revalia — Ethiopian black seed oil, primarily targeting arthritis with many other angles in testing) running direct response video ads on Meta to adults 50+ in the United States. We are hiring a full-time Performance Video Editor & Creative Strategist who can own an ad end to end — concept, script, and edit — not just cut footage together. WHAT THIS ROLE IS: You are not editing vlogs, YouTube videos, or social media content. You are creating direct response video ads that run on cold traffic at real ad spend. Every frame, every transition, every piece of b-roll, every voiceover cut exists for one reason: to keep a skeptical 60-year-old watching long enough to click. If the ad doesn't perform, it gets killed. The creative is the difference between an ad that scales and an ad that dies in testing. This role is not for someone who needs to be handed a script and told what to do. You come up with the concept, write the script, and build the ad yourself. If you have only edited brand content, social media reels, or YouTube videos — or you can only execute other people's ideas — this role is not for you. WHAT YOU WILL DO: You will own the full creative pipeline: concept → script → edit → deliver. One person, full production. On every ad you are making the creative decisions: - Coming up with the concept and angle. You study the brand, the audience, and the mechanism, and you generate ad ideas that will actually convert to cold traffic. - Writing the script yourself. Most ads run 30-60 seconds, but longer formats (up to 3-5 minutes) get made too when the angle calls for it — you use your judgment based on what's working. Hook, body, CTA. You know how a fear-based ad, a discovery ad, a doctor ad, and a personal-story ad each need to be written differently. - Choosing and generating the right b-roll for every section. Not just "find a clip that matches the words." You d ---------- what visual makes the viewer FEEL something at that exact moment. - Pacing the hook so the first 3 seconds stop the scroll. The hook isn't just the first line — it's the first visual, the first sound, the first text on screen, and the speed at which all three hit at once. - Casting the voiceover tone to match the script's intent, selecting music that supports the emotion without competing with the voiceover, designing captions that feel native to the platform, and building transitions the viewer moves through without noticing. You are not editing. You are building ads from a blank page. AI IS NOT OPTIONAL: We use AI tools heavily and daily. This is not a traditional role where you sit in Premiere for 8 hours cutting footage someone else shot. You are generating AI UGC, AI voiceovers, AI b-roll, AI animations, and combining them with real footage to create ads that look and feel authentic. Tools we use include: - Higgsfield for AI video generation, character animation, and b-roll creation - ElevenLabs for AI voiceovers and voice cloning - Runway for motion and visual generation - CapCut or Premiere for editing - Canva for thumbnails and static elements If you are not already using AI tools like these in your daily workflow, this role is not for you. We are not looking for someone "willing to learn AI." We need someone who already generates AI assets as part of how they work. WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT: Most editing jobs hand you footage and say "make it look good." Even most "editor" ad jobs hand you a script and say "make it convert." This role is different — you write the script AND make it convert. You are thinking about performance at every step: - Why does this hook need to hit in under 2 seconds? - Why does the b-roll need to shift at the mechanism section? - Why does the pacing slow down when the product is introduced? - Why does the CTA need urgency without feeling desperate? If you already think like this — as a strategist and an editor at the same time — you will thrive here. WHAT YOU MUST ALREADY HAVE: - Direct response experience — ads that ran on cold traffic for e-commerce, DTC, or supplement brands. Not brand content. Not reels. - The ability to write your own scripts. This is non-negotiable. You will not be handed scripts. You research the angle, write the hook and body, and build the ad from it. - AI-native workflow — you already use Higgsfield, ElevenLabs, Runway or equivalents daily. - Hook psychology — you understand what makes the first 3 seconds stop the scroll and can explain why. - Performance awareness — you know what hook rate, hold rate, CTR, and ROAS mean, and can look at metrics and identify what to change in the next ad. - Health or supplement niche experience preferred — ads for older, health-conscious buyers. You understand this audience responds differently than a 25-year-old buying a gadget. - Strong creative instincts — from a blank page, you know what angle to take, what to write, what b-roll to use, what voice to cast, and how to make it feel like content, not a commercial. THIS ROLE IS NOT: YouTube editing, brand/social content, podcast editing, motion graphics/logo animation, a pure execution role where you wait for scripts, or a junior learn-on-the-job position. If your portfolio is YouTube videos, weddings, vlogs, or brand content — or you can only edit what someone else writes — please do not apply. COMPENSATION AND DETAILS: - Starting at $1,000 USD per month with performance-based increases as your ads prove out - Full-time, 40 hours per week, fully remote - Flexible schedule with daily output expected and end-of-day check-ins via WhatsApp - Long-term position for someone who wants to own the full creative pipeline HOW TO APPLY: Apply only through this Google Form: ----------

title: Freight Dispatcher — U.S. Trucking (Experience Required, Full-Time, Long-Term)
job_title: Freight Dispatcher — U.S. Trucking (Experience Required, Full-Time, Long-Term)
description: About us WH Trucking is a U.S.-based asset carrier operating out of Georgia. We run dedicated contract freight, intermodal/rail moves, and spot loads. We are a small team that moves fast, and you will work directly with the owner. We are hiring four dispatchers to build out 24/7 coverage. This is a long-term position with room to grow as we add trucks. A note on the schedule: our night shift runs 6:00 PM – 6:00 AM U.S. Eastern, which is approximately 6:00 AM – 6:00 PM Philippine time. If you are assigned nights, you will be working normal daytime hours locally. What you'll do Coordinate daily load assignments and driver schedules Communicate with drivers throughout your shift on pickups, deliveries, and delays Manage a dedicated contract account with recurring weekly loads Handle rail/intermodal pickups and in-gate coordination Track loads from pickup through delivery; flag problems before they escalate Collect and file BOLs, PODs, and rate confirmations Maintain dispatch trackers and operational spreadsheets Escalate facility, appointment, and detention issues Support spot load bidding and rate research Hand off cleanly to the incoming dispatcher at shift change Required Prior U.S. freight dispatching experience. This is not negotiable. In your application, name the carriers or brokerages you dispatched for and the fleet size. Strong written and spoken English — you will speak with U.S. drivers and facility staff every shift Confident on the phone, including with frustrated drivers Proficient in Google Workspace (Sheets, Gmail, Drive, Docs) Reliable high-speed internet with a backup connection, and a plan for power outages Quiet, dedicated workspace Self-starter who solves problems rather than forwarding them Nice to have — we will train Amazon Relay experience Intermodal / rail experience (CSX, BNSF) Any TMS experience FMCSA compliance familiarity Small-fleet dispatch experience (as opposed to large carrier) Availability requirements This is a 12-hour shift position on a rotating schedule averaging 42 hours per week, with every other weekend off. Dispatch is a live-coverage role. Trucks, drivers, and facilities do not wait, and no one else can cover your desk while you are away from it. This position requires: Full availability for your entire 12-hour shift, without interruption A dedicated workspace separate from household activity Reliable internet plus a backup connection and a power outage plan No other concurrent job or client work during your shift Consistent attendance — coverage gaps directly affect our customer accounts Willingness to work either day or night rotation as assigned Please be honest with yourself about this before applying. If your current situation does not allow you to be at your desk and responsive for a full 12-hour block, this role will not be a good fit, and we would rather you apply for something that suits your schedule better. HOW TO APPLY To apply, complete BOTH steps. Applications missing either step will not be reviewed. Step 1 — Send your resume and answer in your own words: Which carriers or brokerages have you dispatched for, and how many trucks? Step 2 — Record a Loom video (3 minutes maximum). Record yourself as if you are on the phone with one of our drivers. He has arrived at a rail facility to pick up a load. The kiosk says there is no waybill for his load, so he cannot get in the gate. He has been waiting 40 minutes and he is frustrated. Talk through how you would handle that call and what you would do next. Do not script it. We want to hear how you actually think. Include your Loom link with your application.

title: Receptionist and Intake Coordinator
description: Remote Receptionist & Intake Coordinator U.S. Immigration Law Firm | Full-Time Remote Position | Philippines The Law Offices of Fogam & Associates, LLC, a U.S.-based immigration law firm, is seeking an exceptional Remote Receptionist & Intake Coordinator based in the Philippines. This is a front-line client-service position. You will often be the first person prospective and existing clients speak with. We therefore require excellent spoken and written English, strong listening skills, sound judgment, professionalism, warmth, accuracy, and exceptional reliability. This is not simply a call-answering position. The successful candidate must follow detailed scripts and procedures, listen carefully, obtain and record important information, distinguish between types of calls, identify potentially urgent matters, assist with preliminary intake and qualification, and communicate information promptly and accurately to our U.S. office. Primary Responsibilities • Answer incoming calls promptly, warmly, and professionally. • Follow firm-approved telephone, intake, client-service, qualification, and follow-up scripts. • Listen carefully and ask appropriate scripted follow-up questions. • Accurately document the caller's identity, contact information, reason for calling, important dates/deadlines, requested action, and appropriate next step. • Conduct preliminary intake and qualification of prospective clients using firm procedures. Do not provide legal advice. • Identify promising or time-sensitive prospective-client inquiries and promptly transmit them to the Office Administrator or Operations Manager. • Coordinate or schedule appointments with the Office Administrator or Operations Manager when authorized by firm procedures. • Do not schedule appointments directly with Attorney Fogam and do not represent that you have access to his calendar. • Follow up with prospective clients according to established procedures and scripts. • Route existing-client calls and messages to the appropriate team member. • Recognize potentially urgent situations and immediately escalate them according to the firm's escalation protocol. • Prepare clear, concise written summaries of calls and communications. • Send routine call/activity digests approximately every two hours to the Office Administrator. • Send urgent matters immediately; do not wait for the next two-hour report. • Send qualified or high-priority prospective-client opportunities promptly after the call. • Prepare a detailed end-of-day report accounting for calls, inquiries, follow-ups, unresolved matters, and required next actions. • Maintain strict confidentiality concerning all client and firm information. Communication & Escalation Receptionist → Office Administrator → Operations Manager → Attorney Routine matters should be handled or routed without unnecessarily involving the attorney. Potential emergencies must be escalated immediately. The receptionist should not bypass the chain of responsibility except where a firm procedure specifically requires it. Required Qualifications • Excellent spoken English with clear pronunciation and strong listening comprehension. • Excellent written English. • Ability to understand different accents and callers who may speak imperfect English. • Strong telephone presence and professional demeanor. • Excellent attention to detail and ability to summarize conversations accurately. • Ability to follow scripts without sounding robotic. • Good judgment concerning urgency, priority, and escalation. • Strong computer skills and ability to learn new software. • Reliable high-speed internet, computer, professional headset, and quiet workspace. • Ability to work the required U.S. Eastern Time schedule. • Strong attendance, punctuality, coachability, and confidentiality. Experience as a legal receptionist, intake specialist, virtual assistant, customer-service representative, call-center representative, or with a U.S.-based professional-services organization is preferred but not required. Immigration law experience is helpful but not required. Application Instructions 1. Submit your résumé. 2. Provide a brief written explanation of why you are suited for this position. 3. Submit a 60-90 second audio or video introduction in English explaining your experience and why you would be effective speaking with clients of a U.S. law firm. 4. Provide your internet speed and computer/headset specifications. 5. Confirm that you can work the required U.S. Eastern Time schedule. Selected applicants will complete a short written/computer assessment and telephone role-playing exercises. Please do not apply if you are uncomfortable spending substantial portions of the workday speaking with clients and prospective clients by telephone.

title: Partner Network Lead – Philippines
description: ABOUT US Bees Mobile is a digital communications service providing virtual phone numbers (US / HK) and travel eSIM data. Our customers are people like your friends and family: · VAs and freelancers who need a US number so international clients take them seriously · OFWs who need to keep an active number for OTP and bank messages · Travelers who want internet the moment they land The service is live and selling. Growth comes through a partner program: people who share the service with their network and earn from the customers and partners they bring in. Bees Mobile is now opening the Philippine market and hiring a small founding team to build the partner network from zero. ───────────────────────────── THE ROLE You will build the Bees Mobile partner network in the Philippines. Not one customer at a time — you find people who can build teams, bring them in, train them, and help them grow. If you have built a direct-selling or network-marketing organization before, you already know this job. If you have led a large team of agents, resellers, or freelancers and know how to keep them active, you know most of it. WHAT YOU WILL DO · Recruit partners across the Philippines — both experienced team leaders (direct-selling leaders, insurance unit managers, reseller and agent network heads) and motivated newcomers who want to start · Run online presentations (Zoom / Messenger / FB Live) to explain the service and partner program — materials provided · Onboard and train new partners using the handbook, videos, and scripts · Keep partners active: regular check-ins, answer questions, solve problems · Monitor what partners post and make sure it follows the communication standards · Work with the marketing team on local campaigns: you tell them what works in the Philippines and what doesn't · Track your numbers and send a weekly report to head office ───────────────────────────── HOW THE TRIAL WORKS A small founding team starts on a 3-month paid trial with clear, written targets. Strong performers convert to permanent roles with a higher base salary. title: VIP Client Support Associate
description: We're building a remote VIP Support team for a Japan-based fintech platform, and we're looking for people we can grow from the ground up — not just workers, but the kind of people who take genuine pride in doing things right. This role blends support with relationship-building: you won't just resolve client concerns, you'll also learn to spot the right moments to introduce clients to more of what we offer. This is not a call center role. You'll be managing real relationships with high-value clients — providing support, but also recognizing opportunities to grow those relationships — and holding yourself to a high standard on every single interaction. Our clients are VIPs — quality is the only standard. We train every associate to think critically and work out the correct response on their own, using AI as a support tool rather than a substitute for judgment. Once you've proven you can consistently get it right, you'll be trusted to move fast — real speed is earned through skill, not shortcuts. We're a growing team, and we mean that literally — the processes, tools, and structure you'll work with are still being shaped, and we actively want people who take initiative to help shape them. The culture here is built on mutual trust, shared accountability, and a genuine respect for doing things well. If that resonates with you, keep reading. Responsibilities: • Handle inbound client inquiries via messaging platforms with care and thoroughness • Recognize natural opportunities within conversations to introduce clients to relevant features, promotions, or products that genuinely add value to them • Use our drafting tool to sharpen your own well-considered responses for supervisor review — the tool supports your judgment; it doesn't replace it • Keep thorough, accurate track of each client's concerns and history — nothing gets forgotten, nothing falls through the cracks • Escalate immediately to your Lead when handling an irate or escalating client — do not attempt to resolve it alone • Maintain detailed and accurate client interaction logs • Follow team rules, protocols, and procedures diligently — structure exists for a reason and will be respected • We believe every client interaction is a once-in-a-lifetime encounter that deserves your full presence and care. What We're Looking For: • Early career — fresh graduates welcome, but you need real client-facing experience (internship, part-time work, thesis project, VA work, or similar counts) • High energy and quick on your feet — comfortable with fast, informal communication (voice notes, memes, Slack chaos included) and unfazed by a startup's rough edges • Confident — you speak up, express yourself clearly, and don't go quiet when things get uncomfortable • Understands hierarchy — you know when to handle something yourself and when to bring it to your Lead, and you act without being told • Conscientious — you track every detail, follow through, and take full ownership of every client you handle • Relationship-minded — you can naturally spot opportunities to add value for a client, not just resolve their immediate issue • Follows rules diligently — protocols aren't suggestions • Strong written English — clear, warm, and professional • Sharp critical thinking — you can reason through a client's situation yourself, not just reword what a tool gives you • Comfortable using AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, or similar) as an aid, not a crutch • High discretion — you'll be handling sensitive VIP information • Startup mindset — adaptable, steady, and not easily rattled Bonus Points (not required, but we will prioritize you): • Holds a TESDA BPO NC II certification • HubSpot or Zendesk Customer Service certification • Google AI Essentials or equivalent AI literacy certificate • JLPT N2/N1 or business-level fluency — especially valuable if you can review Japanese-language drafts for tone and accuracy • Familiar with crypto, DeFi, or fintech products • Experience in sales, account management, upselling, or client retention • Has handled foreign or executive-level clients before Reporting to: VIP Support Lead and Growth Operations Lead Setup: • 100% WFH from day one • 8 AM–4 PM Philippine Time (JST business hours) to start, 5 days/week — this window may extend depending on client traffic and business needs, so come in with realistic expectations around hours • No time tracker • Overtime available as needed and subject to supervisor approval • Team communication via Slack • BYOD — stable fiber internet required • Confidentiality/NDA agreement required before you handle any client information • Paid training and evaluation period — Part-Time status, working full 8-hour days, running through the 30th of the month you're hired (this lines up with our salary reporting cycle) • Promotion to Full-Time is based on your evaluation — if your performance is clearly solid early on, that promotion can happen before the 30th too • Initiative is welcomed — stepping up when it's needed is part of the culture here • Internal growth and promotions for top performers To Apply: Start your message with the subject line: [VIP Support] – [Your Name] – [City] Then answer all three questions below. We read every response personally — take your time with these. 1. You're handling five VIP clients at the same time. One sends you a voice note. One sends a meme with no context. One hasn't replied in 3 days and suddenly needs urgent help. One says "???" and one says "never mind." Walk us through your exact next 10 minutes. 2. If we give you a chance at this role, what is the one thing you can promise us? 3. Think of a time you were part of a startup or company — what's one initiative you personally established that's still in use today (or was used before you left), and became part of how that company actually operates? A note on AI: using it to help you write is fine — we use it ourselves. But we can tell when an answer wasn't reviewed by the person sending it. Edit before you submit. Important: Do not use any of the following words anywhere in your application — passionate, dedicated, hardworking, committed, team player, fast learner, or go-getter. Applications containing these words will not be reviewed. We want your real voice, not resume language. Applications without the correct subject line and all three answers will not be reviewed.

This is a viral content strategist role with real performance bonuses for every post that goes viral. What You'll Do - Produce content manually when workflows need fixes or adjustments - Manage and troubleshoot complex N8N workflows that power the entire content pipeline - Optimize AI prompts and wildcards daily to maximize content quality and viral potential - Analyze content performance and identify what works per creator, then scale those patterns - Build and maintain a database of proven viral content formats - Ensure every piece of content stays on-brand for each creator's personality and niche - Research viral formats and translate them into our automated systems - Scale what works, which is 90% of output, and test new creative formats, which is 10% Current state: We clone proven viral formats from other creators, adapted to our own brands. The process is largely automated but needs daily management and optimization. Where we're going: A fully creative pipeline that generates original viral concepts from scratch. You'll steer an AI content engine, not just manage it. Who You Are Viral content expert: You have made content go viral before, multiple times, with proof. You understand hooks, emotional triggers, share psychology, and format structures. You know that viral on Facebook means shares. You can look at any piece of content and predict whether it will perform, and explain exactly why. AI prompting specialist: You work daily with LLMs such as ChatGPT and Claude. You write structured prompts that produce consistent, high-quality output. You understand prompt engineering as a real skill. Experience with AI image and video generation prompting is required. N8N / automation operator: You have worked with N8N or similar tools such as Make or Zapier. You can read, debug, and modify complex workflows independently. You are comfortable with JSON, webhooks, and troubleshooting integrations. Brand builder: You know how to build and maintain a consistent brand and personality from scratch. Every post must feel like it comes from the same person, even at scale. Social native: You understand the social media algorithm, what makes users share, and how Reels distribution works. Organized and independent: You track your own work without being managed. You document what you do. You flag issues before they become problems. You'll Thrive Here If - You are obsessed with understanding why content goes viral, not just watching it happen - You love optimizing systems by changing one variable, measuring the result, and improving again - You are comfortable with bold and provocative content aimed at mature audiences - You get excited about AI tools and automation, and see them as creative leverage, not just tech - You want to grow with a business, not just fill a seat - You think in data and patterns, not feelings and guesses You'll Struggle Here If - You have never made content go viral and cannot show proof - You are uncomfortable working with mature or provocative content - You need step-by-step instructions for every task - You see AI as a gimmick rather than a production tool - You want a predictable 9-to-5 with no ambition beyond the base salary - You have another job or freelance work alongside this role, because this must be your only commitment - You avoid troubleshooting technical issues and wait for someone else to fix things Why Join Us? Compensation - Base: $400/month for 40 hours/week, Monday to Friday - Viral bonuses: paid per post that crosses performance thresholds of 25K, 100K, or 500K likes - With hundreds of posts going out monthly, strong performers consistently earn $1000+ in monthly bonuses on top of base - As the operation scales, hours and compensation grow with it Growth - You are joining at the ground floor of a scaling AI content operation - The role evolves from managing cloned content today to steering a fully creative AI content engine - We need someone who grows into a leadership role as we expand What You Get to Work With - Cutting-edge AI tools for image and video generation - Fully automated N8N content pipelines - A tested viral format database and content strategy How to Apply Generic applications will be ignored. Attach your CV with your previous work experience, and answer all of the following: 1. Viral proof Share content you personally created or were directly responsible for that got significant reach. 2. Platform experience List every social media platform you have professional experience with. For each platform, include your role, how long you worked on it, and the best result you achieved, such as followers grown, views on a single post, or engagement rate.

title: AI Video Editor — DTC Creative Ads (Realistic AI Generation)
job_title: AI Video Editor — DTC Creative Ads (Realistic AI Generation)
description: The Role We're a DTC brand that lives and dies by creative, and we're looking for an AI video editor who can generate highly realistic, believable AI video — not the uncanny, obviously-synthetic stuff, but footage and avatars that hold up as real ad creative in the feed. You'll turn prompts, product assets, and UGC into scroll-stopping ads for Meta, TikTok, and YouTube, using AI generation to produce content that would be slow, expensive, or impossible to shoot. This is a craft-plus-volume role. The bar is realism: if your AI-generated humans, environments, and product shots pass as authentic and convert like real footage, you'll thrive here. What You'll Own Generating photorealistic AI video — lifelike avatars/spokespeople, realistic environments, and product footage that reads as genuine, not synthetic. Editing direct-response ad creative for Meta, TikTok, and YouTube — hooks, UGC-style edits, VSLs, listicles, and demos built to convert. High-volume variant production — spinning winning concepts into many testable variations (hooks, avatars, scenes, captions, pacing, CTAs, aspect ratios). Realism QA — catching and fixing the tells that break believability: warped hands, off lip-sync, unnatural motion, lighting mismatches, artifacting. Format discipline — native 9:16, 4:5, and 1:1 cuts optimized per placement. What You Bring A portfolio of highly realistic AI-generated video — this is the core requirement. Show us AI footage or avatars that are hard to clock as synthetic. Deep, hands-on command of AI video generation tools — e.g., Kling, Seedance, Veo, HeyGen/Synthesia (realistic avatars), ElevenLabs (voice/lip-sync) — and the prompting and post skills to push each toward realism. Strong editing and compositing fundamentals (Premiere, After Effects, DaVinci, CapCut) to grade, retime, clean up, and blend AI output into a seamless finished ad. A real point of view on DTC / direct-response creative — hooks, retention, sound-off editing, and why the first 3 seconds matter. Sharp eye for the details that separate believable AI from uncanny, plus speed and consistency at volume. Nice to Have Motion graphics/VFX and compositing chops, custom avatar or voice-clone creation, image-to-video and upscaling workflows (e.g., Topaz), familiarity with Meta/TikTok ad and AI-disclosure policies, and a sense for testing angles. How to Apply Send your portfolio with: your most realistic AI-generated clip (and how you made it), a DTC ad you edited that performed well, and a rough sense of how many ad variants you can turn around in a week.

title: SEO Blog Content Writer & Content Strategist – Webflow + Canva
job_title: SEO Blog Content Writer & Content Strategist – Webflow + Canva
description: We are looking for a **creative, SEO-focused blog writer and content strategist** who can take ownership of our ongoing website content. This role is not simply about being handed a topic and writing an article. We need someone who understands **how to research keywords, identify topics worth ranking for, build a long-term content plan, write engaging and useful articles, create supporting graphics, and publish finished content directly to our website.** The ideal person is both **creative and analytical**. You should be able to look at our business, services, target customers, and competitors and develop a roadmap of blog topics designed to increase organic traffic and generate leads. ## What You'll Be Responsible For ### SEO Keyword & Topic Research * Research keywords relevant to our services, customers, and geographic markets. * Identify search terms with realistic ranking opportunities. * Understand search intent and determine what someone is actually looking for when searching a keyword. * Find long-tail keyword opportunities and supporting topics. * Research competitor websites and identify content gaps. * Determine which topics should be prioritized based on traffic potential, competition, and business value. ### Content Strategy & Blog Mapping You should be comfortable creating an organized **content roadmap rather than writing random individual blog posts.** This includes: * Creating monthly and quarterly blog topic plans. * Building topic clusters around our primary services. * Identifying pillar articles and supporting articles. * Mapping related articles together for internal linking. * Avoiding keyword cannibalization between articles. * Developing location-specific content when appropriate. * Planning evergreen content as well as seasonal or timely content. * Recommending updates to older articles when opportunities exist. We want someone who can essentially say: **"Here are the keywords we should target, here are the articles we should create around them, and here is the order we should publish them."** ## Blog Writing You will be responsible for writing polished, engaging articles that are both **optimized for search engines and enjoyable for real people to read.** Articles should include: * Strong SEO-friendly titles. * Clear introductions that quickly answer the reader's question. * Logical H1, H2, and H3 structure. * Natural keyword placement. * Related keywords and supporting topics. * Internal links to relevant website pages and blog posts. * Appropriate external references when necessary. * Calls to action that naturally lead readers toward our services. * Meta titles and meta descriptions. * Suggested URL slugs. * Image alt text. * FAQ sections when appropriate. Content should never feel robotic, repetitive, overly keyword-stuffed, or written simply to satisfy an SEO checklist. ## Creative Writing Ability We want someone capable of understanding the personality of a business and writing content that sounds **natural, knowledgeable, professional, and approachable.** You should be able to: * Take technical or boring subjects and make them interesting. * Develop strong hooks and introductions. * Tell stories when appropriate. * Explain complicated subjects simply. * Match an existing company's voice and writing style. * Understand the difference between educational content and promotional content. * Write content designed to build trust rather than constantly selling. * Come up with creative angles for subjects that competitors may already be covering. ## Webflow Experience You should have experience working with **Webflow CMS** or be comfortable learning and working directly inside a structured CMS. Responsibilities may include: * Creating new blog posts inside Webflow. * Formatting headings, paragraphs, lists, links, and images. * Selecting categories and tags. * Adding SEO titles and meta descriptions. * Creating clean URL slugs. * Adding featured images. * Adding image alt descriptions. * Previewing articles before publishing. * Checking desktop and mobile formatting. * Connecting internal links throughout the website. * Scheduling or publishing completed articles. You should be comfortable working independently inside an established website without a ---------- changing unrelated website elements. ## Canva & Basic Graphic Design Blog posts will also require supporting imagery. You should have experience using **Canva or similar design software** to create professional-looking blog graphics. This may include: * Combining multiple photos into one graphic. * Creating featured blog images. * Cropping and resizing photographs. * Adding text overlays when appropriate. * Removing or replacing backgrounds. * Creating simple comparison graphics. * Creating informational graphics. * Maintaining consistent fonts, branding, spacing, and visual style. * Exporting properly optimized images for web use. You do not need to be a professional graphic designer, but you should have **a good visual eye and understand what makes something look polished and professional.** ## Understanding of Modern SEO Candidates should understand concepts including: * Keyword research. * Search intent. * Long-tail keywords. * Keyword difficulty. * Search volume. * Topical authority. * Content clusters. * Internal linking. * On-page SEO. * Local SEO. * Meta descriptions. * Title tags. * Image optimization. * Alt text. * Featured snippets. * FAQ content. * Competitor research. * Content gap analysis. * Updating and refreshing existing content. Experience with SEO tools such as **Ahrefs, Semrush, Google Search Console, Google Analytics, Keyword Planner, Screaming Frog, or similar platforms** is strongly preferred. ## AI-Assisted Writing We are comfortable with AI tools being used as part of the research and writing process. However, we are **not looking for someone who simply generates an article with AI and publishes it.** The person in this role must know how to: * Research and verify information. * Fact-check AI-generated material. * Rewrite content so it sounds natural. * Remove generic or repetitive AI language. * Add original insight and business-specific information. * Maintain a consistent company voice. * Recognize when AI-generated information is inaccurate. * Use AI as a productivity tool rather than a replacement for writing and strategy. ## Required Skills The ideal candidate will have: * Strong English writing and grammar skills. * Previous SEO blog-writing experience. * Experience performing keyword and competitor research. * Experience creating content calendars or SEO content strategies. * Understanding of search intent. * Experience publishing content through a CMS. * Webflow experience or strong experience with similar CMS platforms. * Canva or basic graphic-design experience. * Strong attention to detail. * Ability to work independently. * Ability to meet deadlines and maintain an organized content schedule. * Ability to research unfamiliar industries and quickly understand them. * Ability to follow an established brand voice. ## Strong Candidates Will Also Understand * Local-service SEO. * Service-area businesses. * Conversion-focused website writing. * Google Business Profile strategy. * Schema and structured content. * Google Search Console. * Google Analytics. * Content performance reporting. * Basic image SEO. * Basic website UX. * Content repurposing for social media. * How blog content supports service and landing pages. ## What We Don't Want We are not looking for someone who: * Only writes when given an exact topic. * Depends entirely on AI-generated articles. * Produces generic 500-word SEO posts. * Keyword-stuffs articles. * Copies competitor content. * Publishes articles without checking formatting. * Requires detailed instructions for every assignment. * Focuses exclusively on search volume without understanding whether a keyword could actually generate customers. We want someone who can **think strategically and bring ideas to us.** ## Example of the Workflow A typical project may look like this: 1. Review one of our primary services. 2. Research keywords and competing websites. 3. Identify 10–30 potential article opportunities. 4. Organize those articles into a content cluster. 5. Recommend which articles should be written first. 6. Write the article. 7. Create or prepare the supporting images. 8. Optimize the article for SEO. 9. Add internal links. 10. Publish the article in Webflow. 11. Review the finished page on desktop and mobile. 12. Track performance and recommend future content based on results. ## When Applying Please include: * Examples of blog articles you have written. * Examples of websites where you have published content. * Your experience with SEO keyword research. * SEO tools you regularly use. * Your experience with Webflow. * Examples of graphics you have created in Canva. * An example of a content calendar, keyword map, or content strategy you have created. * A short explanation of how you d ---------- whether a keyword is worth targeting. * Your preferred pricing structure: hourly, per article, or monthly retainer. ### Bonus Application Question Imagine we are trying to rank a local service business for a competitive primary keyword. Briefly explain how you would turn that **one main keyword into a 3-month blog content strategy.** We are specifically looking for someone who can combine **SEO strategy + creative writing + visual content + Webflow publishing** and become an ongoing part of our content marketing process.

title: Senior Graphic Designer & Photoshop Artist
description: # Senior Graphic Designer & Photoshop Artist We are looking for a **high-level Senior Graphic Designer and Photoshop Artist** with exceptional creative ability, advanced photo-editing skills, and a strong understanding of professional visual design. This is **not an entry-level position** and is not a role for someone who primarily relies on Canva templates, pre-made designs, or AI-generated artwork. We are looking for someone who can start with raw photographs, brand assets, logos, text, and a creative direction and build a **polished, professional finished design from scratch using Adobe Photoshop and other professional Adobe tools.** You should be equally comfortable creating a completely new design as you are taking an existing image and transforming it into something dramatically better. ## What You'll Be Creating Projects may include: * Website graphics * Blog featured images * Social media graphics * Advertising graphics * Promotional materials * Event graphics * Digital advertisements * Flyers * Posters * Sales materials * Service graphics * Photo composites * Before-and-after graphics * Website banners and hero images * Branded marketing materials * YouTube thumbnails * Presentation graphics * Print-ready marketing materials The work will vary significantly, so we need someone who can **think creatively rather than simply follow templates.** ## Advanced Photoshop Skills Are Required Photoshop will be a major part of this position. You should have advanced experience with: * Professional photo retouching * Skin retouching while maintaining natural texture * Color correction * Color grading * Exposure correction * Object removal * Background removal * Background replacement * Hair masking and detailed selections * Layer masks * Adjustment layers * Smart Objects * Blend modes * Advanced selections * Perspective correction * Image reconstruction * Compositing multiple photographs * Matching lighting between multiple images * Matching color between multiple photographs * Creating realistic shadows * Creating realistic reflections * Cleaning distracting elements from photographs * Extending or rebuilding backgrounds * Product and equipment retouching * Creating depth and separation within compositions * Preparing graphics for web and print * Non-destructive Photoshop workflows You should be capable of combining **several completely different photographs into one image and making the final composition look intentional and believable.** ## Photo Compositing A major part of this position involves taking existing photography and turning it into professional marketing imagery. For example, you may be provided: * A photograph of a person * A photograph of an event * A photograph of equipment * A venue photograph * Logos * Brand assets * Text * Multiple reference images You may then need to combine those elements into **one cohesive advertisement or marketing graphic.** We need someone who understands: * Light direction * Perspective * Scale * Depth * Shadows * Highlights * Color temperature * Image resolution * Composition The finished graphic should not look like several photographs pasted together. It should look like **one professionally created image.** ## Graphic Design Skills Beyond Photoshop ability, you must have a strong understanding of professional graphic design. You should understand: * Visual hierarchy * Typography * Font pairing * Spacing * Alignment * Composition * Negative space * Contrast * Balance * Brand consistency * Color theory * Layout * Advertising design * Marketing design * Designing for different aspect ratios * Designing for mobile versus desktop * Creating graphics that communicate quickly and clearly We are looking for someone who understands the difference between something that is simply **technically correct** and something that actually **looks great.** ## Creative Direction We do not want to provide exact instructions for every design. Sometimes you may receive a project that simply says: **"We need a graphic promoting this service. Here are the photos, logo, and information."** You should be able to determine: * What photographs should be used * Which photographs should not be used * How the composition should be structured * Where the viewer's eye should go first * What information should be emphasized * How much text should appear * What typography works best * How the brand should be represented * Whether the design needs to feel luxury, energetic, corporate, modern, dramatic, clean, etc. A senior designer should be able to **bring creative ideas to the project rather than waiting for every creative decision to be made for them.** ## Adobe Creative Suite Advanced Photoshop experience is mandatory. Experience with the following is also highly preferred: * Adobe Illustrator * Adobe InDesign * Adobe Lightroom * Adobe Acrobat * Adobe Bridge Illustrator experience is particularly valuable for: * Vector graphics * Logo manipulation * Icons * Typography * Print graphics * Scalable design elements ## No AI-Generated Design **We are specifically looking for traditional professional design and photo-editing skills.** Generative AI should **not** be used to create finished artwork, photographs, backgrounds, people, equipment, or design elements for our projects unless specifically authorized. We want someone who understands how to actually use Photoshop. You should be capable of performing professional: * Selections * Masking * Retouching * Compositing * Color correction * Background replacement * Image manipulation * Typography * Layout without depending on AI to create the work for you. Our goal is to maintain control over the quality, accuracy, branding, and authenticity of our imagery. ## Senior-Level Expectations Because this is a senior position, you should be able to: * Take ownership of projects. * Work from limited creative direction. * Develop multiple strong concepts when needed. * Explain why you made specific design decisions. * Recognize when an image or concept isn't working. * Maintain consistency across an entire brand. * Work quickly without sacrificing quality. * Organize Photoshop files professionally. * Maintain clean layers and editable source files. * Follow established naming and file-management systems. * Prepare files correctly for web, social media, and print. * Review your own work before submitting it. * Catch spelling, alignment, resolution, and formatting problems. * Receive creative feedback professionally and make revisions efficiently. ## Required Qualifications Candidates should have: * **5+ years of professional graphic design experience preferred.** * Advanced Adobe Photoshop skills. * Strong professional portfolio. * Extensive photo-editing experience. * Extensive photo-compositing experience. * Strong typography and layout skills. * Understanding of professional branding. * Experience creating marketing and advertising graphics. * Understanding of print and digital design. * Excellent attention to detail. * Strong creative judgment. * Ability to work independently. * Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines. * Ability to follow established brand standards. ## What We're NOT Looking For This position is probably not the right fit if your primary experience is: * Canva templates * AI image generation * AI-generated advertisements * Template-based social media design * Basic Photoshop editing * Simple background removal * Drag-and-drop graphic creation Those tools have their place, but this position requires someone with **professional-level Photoshop and graphic-design skills.** We need someone who can actually build, edit, manipulate, and refine the artwork. ## Portfolio Requirements **A portfolio is required.** Your portfolio should demonstrate actual professional design work and preferably include: * Photo composites * Before-and-after photo editing * Advertising graphics * Marketing graphics * Website graphics * Social media campaigns * Event or entertainment graphics * Professional retouching * Typography-focused designs * Photoshop-heavy projects We are particularly interested in seeing projects where you took **multiple source photographs or assets and created an entirely new finished composition.** ## When Applying Please provide: * A link to your portfolio. * How many years you have worked professionally as a graphic designer. * Your level of Photoshop experience. * The Adobe programs you regularly use. * Examples of your strongest Photoshop compositing work. * Examples of professional photo retouching. * Examples of marketing or advertising designs. * Your normal turnaround time for design projects. * Whether you work hourly, per project, or on a recurring monthly basis. * Your availability. Please also tell us which **three projects in your portfolio best demonstrate your Photoshop ability** and briefly explain what you personally did to create each image. ## Potential Skills Test Final candidates may be given a **paid design test** using photographs and assets supplied by us. The purpose of the test is not simply to see whether you can use Photoshop. We want to evaluate your: * Creativity * Composition * Photo-editing ability * Attention to detail * Typography * Ability to follow a brand * Ability to interpret creative direction * Layer organization * Overall professional judgment We're looking for a designer whose work makes someone stop and say: **"That looks professionally done."** If you are a highly experienced designer who genuinely enjoys Photoshop, photo manipulation, compositing, and creating polished visual marketing materials from scratch, we'd like to see your work.
