title: Youtube Senior Editor
description: We are looking for an expert-level YouTube Video Editor who can create premium, retention-focused long-form content for top creators and brands. This role is best suited for editors who understand high-quality YouTube storytelling in the style of channels such as Vox, Johnny Harris, Cleo Abram, and other documentary/explainer-style creators. We are not looking for basic editors, short-form-only editors, or editors who simply add cuts and captions. We are looking for someone with strong creative judgment, technical skill, and the ability to turn raw footage and direction into a polished, engaging, and thoughtful YouTube video. The ideal editor understands pacing, story structure, audience retention, visual clarity, motion graphics, sound design, and how every editing choice affects the viewer’s experience. Responsibilities Edit high-quality long-form YouTube videos for creators, brands, and educational content. Build strong hooks that make viewers want to keep watching. Shape raw footage into a clear and engaging story. Use B-roll, archival footage, graphics, music, sound design, and visual references intentionally. Create clean motion graphics, maps, text animations, callouts, and visual explanations when needed. Improve pacing, flow, clarity, and retention throughout the video. Follow creative direction while also bringing your own strong editorial judgment. Apply feedback quickly and professionally. Work with creative leads, producers, and post-production teams to meet high creative standards. Deliver polished edits on time in a fast-moving YouTube-first environment. Qualifications Strong experience editing long-form YouTube videos. Expert-level skill in Adobe Premiere Pro. Expert-level skill in Adobe After Effects and motion graphics. Good understanding of Photoshop or other Adobe Creative Suite tools. Strong storytelling and pacing instincts. Ability to create documentary, explainer, talking-head, educational, or creator-style edits. Strong use of B-roll, archival footage, visual references, graphics, sound design, and music. Understanding of audience retention, viewer engagement, and YouTube performance. Experience editing high-performing or high-quality content for creators, agencies, brands, or media companies. Ability to work with feedback, revisions, and tight deadlines. Strong attention to detail and clean technical execution. Reliable computer/workstation setup and strong internet connection. This Role Is Not For Entry-level editors. Editors with only short-form reel experience. Editors with only wedding, corporate, event, or basic social media editing experience. Editors who are not comfortable with long-form YouTube content. Editors who only follow instructions but do not bring creative judgment. Editors who cannot work with feedback or tight deadlines. Editors who do not have strong Premiere Pro and After Effects skills. Benefits Work from anywhere! We’re a 100% remote team. A quarterly wellness reimbursement 20 days of paid time off annually. 12 additional holidays per year. Unlimited sick and bereavement leave. Working for a company that is values-oriented and committed to positive social impact. Unlimited reimbursement on book purchases for self-education. Gifts/cash bonuses on birthdays, work anniversaries, and other work-related achievements. Working directly with some of the largest brands on the planet. Additionally, Dragonfruit is highly committed to offering all our team members opportunities for growth and mobility within the company. This could include moving up to Lead Short-Form or Long-Form Editor, Director of the Editing Department, Post-Production Supervisor, or even Creative Director or beyond! (Of course, all of these positions come with pay increases.) ? If you're ready to join Dragonfruit and play a role in the future of YouTube, submit your application now! ----------

description: About Rinse & Rise Atlanta Rinse & Rise Atlanta is a growing residential and commercial cleaning company serving customers throughout the Atlanta, Georgia area. We receive leads from Google, Yelp, referrals, outbound prospecting, real estate professionals, and other marketing channels. We are looking for an experienced sales professional who can take ownership of these leads and convert them into confirmed cleaning appointments. Important selling points include: • Customers do not pay until the cleaning has been completed • If a customer is not satisfied, we will return and address the cleaning concerns at no additional charge • Our professional cleaners have extensive cleaning experience • We provide residential, recurring, move-in/move-out, Airbnb, post-construction, and commercial cleaning services • Customers receive responsive communication and dependable service You will be trained on our pricing, services, policies, guarantees, and approved negotiation limits. What We’re Looking For • At least 3 years of phone sales, inbound sales, appointment-setting, or lead-conversion experience • A proven ability to convert inquiries into appointments or sales • Previous cleaning-company or home-service sales experience is strongly preferred • Experience speaking with U.S.-based customers • Excellent spoken and written English • A confident, friendly, persuasive, and professional phone presence • Strong listening and objection-handling skills • Comfortable discussing pricing and directly asking customers to book • Persistent with follow-ups without becoming aggressive or unprofessional • Able to learn new services, pricing structures, and policies quickly • Organized and comfortable using Google Sheets, email, SMS, and online lead platforms • Reliable high-speed internet, quiet workspace, and high-quality headset • Available during U.S. Eastern Time business hours What We Provide • Training on our services, pricing, policies, and guarantees • Approved pricing ranges and negotiation guidelines • Sales scripts and objection-handling materials • Role-play training before handling live calls • Business phone and messaging systems • Inbound leads and outbound prospect lists • A structured lead-tracking and follow-up process • Direct access to the business owner • Opportunities for additional hours and performance-based compensation Schedule Approximately 20 hours per week to start, primarily during U.S. Eastern Time business hours. Performance bonuses may be provided for confirmed bookings and strong conversion results. Outstanding performance may lead to higher compensation, additional hours, and a long-term position with the company. title: Real Estate Deal Analyst — Multi-Unit Acquisitions & Development Land
job_title: Real Estate Deal Analyst — Multi-Unit Acquisitions & Development Land
description: We are a Canadian real-estate firm: we analyse what is on the market, find the deals that actually work, and bring them to a group of investors who buy them. On the development side, investors buy land and retain us to build on it. We have built something unusual. Our deal engine pulls the licensed feed and run full development pro formas, financing paths, cost models, returns — and ranks them. It runs unattended while we sleep. Here is the honest problem, and it is the reason this job exists: that engine is not able to produce a complete deal package. Not because the analysis is wrong. Because the analysis stops at the edge of what public data can tell you. To finish a deal you need the rent roll, the T12, the operating statement, the capex history. Those live in a listing agent's inbox, and somebody has to ask for them, chase them, read them properly, and record them in a separate system. Analyze, package them, and send to our investors. That gap is the job. What you'll own 1. The seller side. Contact listing agents on the deals our engine ranks. Request rent rolls, T12s, operating statements, condition and capex history. Chase what doesn't arrive. Read what does and d ---------- whether it is complete, thin, or evasive. 2. The underwrite. Put real numbers, supply the per-deal inputs it refuses to invent, and interrogate what comes back. The engine tells you what is still missing — your job is to close that gap or conclude the deal is dead and say why. 3. The package. Produce the document our investors d ---------- on: the thesis, the numbers, the risks, the recommendation, the price. 4. The buyer side. Answer our investors' questions on the packages you produce — what is in the numbers, what the risks are, what we know and what we don't. Keep that side organised too: who has seen what, who is interested in which lane, who asked what, who is still waiting on you. 5. Your own record. You bring or build your own way of tracking all of it — deals live, deals dead and why, documents requested and outstanding, investors and their questions. We are not going to hand you a CRM and we do not want to. Bring yours. Both lanes from day one: existing multi-unit buildings, and development land. What is not yours Negotiating price or terms, advising an investor on what to pay, and presenting offers are licensed acts. The owner holds the licence and does those. You gather, organise, analyse, and answer questions about the deal; he advises and trades. We would rather draw that line clearly now than have it blur later. Hours Email is asynchronous and so is most of this work. You do not need to work Atlantic Canada hours. There is no graveyard shift. You do need some overlapping hours as you would be expected to call/text people. What matters is that agents and investors get timely, professional replies and that nothing sits for days. What you get A deal engine that has already done the heavy analytical work, so you are not building models from scratch in a spreadsheet. Claude Code and AI tooling, with the expectation that you automate your own workflow — and we pay for what you need. Direct access to the owner, who holds the local domain knowledge and will teach it. Who fits 1. You are relentlessly organised, and you build the systems that keep you that way. This is the most important thing on this page. You will be holding three sets of moving parts at once: the deals themselves, the seller side (which agent, which documents asked for, which still outstanding, who has gone quiet), and the buyer side (which investor saw which package, what they asked, what they are waiting on). If any of that lives only in your head or your inbox, this falls apart. We want to see the tracker, CRM or pipeline you have actually built and run. 2. Real estate transaction experience on the broker side is a major bonus. If you have worked inside a brokerage — transaction management, deal administration, listing or buyer-side support — say so early. You will already know what documents exist, who holds them, and how long they take to prise loose. 3. The mathematics are not the hard part. Cap rates, NOI and a pro forma are arithmetic, and our engine does most of it.What is hard, and what we are actually testing, is whether you can look at a set of numbers and tell that they have been dressed up. You do not need to know our local market. Our system encodes the local planning rules, financing programs and cost models. The owner holds the rest and will teach it. You reach for automation by instinct. Not a developer — someone who, handed Claude, builds themselves a system rather than asking for one. Who doesn't This is not a virtual assistant, executive assistant, or admin role, and applications framed that way will not be read. If your instinct is to perfect the system before producing output, this will frustrate you — we have a great deal of system and little completed deals, and the balance needs to move the other way. If you pass information along without concluding anything, we have hired that before and will not do it again. To apply Put HALYARD as the first word of your application. Then three things. title: AI Systems Builder / Automation Engineer / Full-Stack Dev
job_title: AI Systems Builder / Automation Engineer / Full-Stack Dev
description: I'm a British entrepreneur based in Thailand running multiple ventures: ScaleSage (an AI Systems & Automation Specialists agency), a Caribbean restaurant in Pattaya (Belly Full), a Caribbean seasoning brand launching into UK retail with production in China (Belly Full Seasonings), a kids' education app (Legacy Curriculum), and internal AI systems for algorithmic trading and business automation. I operate through voice-to-text, Claude, and Claude Code — I architect systems and my team executes. My bottleneck isn't strategy, it's execution bandwidth. I already have an EA (Cy, Filipino, doing strong work). I now need a technical counterpart — someone who can use AI tools, APIs, and automations to build the systems my businesses run on. I'm a founder, not a big corporation. This means two things: I can move fast and make decisions without red tape, and I pay what's fair without corporate budgets to throw around. The trade-off is real opportunity — the right person here grows with me as the businesses grow. I'm not necessarily looking for an elite "senior AI engineer" who needs $3,000/month. I'm looking for a hungry, AI-native technical builder — mid-high level technically, senior in hunger. Someone who uses existing models, APIs, automations, and tools to ship working business systems fast. HOW THIS WORKS I want to start someone part-time (20-25 hours/week) for the first month as a paid trial. This protects both of us — we find out if we click without either side being locked in. If the fit is right and the work justifies it, we move to full-time hours over time. Nothing is promised. Everything is earned. IF we click, IF the work ethic is there, IF the fit is right — this role has real growth potential. Performance is everything. Bonuses are paid for execution, reliability, speed, and quality — when you ship a big build, solve a complex problem, or hit a real performance milestone. Pay rises are earned through consistency, loyalty, and reliability over time. Eventually leading a small dev / tech team as we scale. We aim for high standards and quality constantly. We don't ship sub-standard work. I'd rather you ship less, cleanly, than rush something half-built. Shortcuts cost us more than slow shipping ever will. The right person here takes pride in their craft and signs their name on what they ship. I won't sell you a dream. I'll tell you the ceiling is high for the right person. WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY DO Trial month — full ScaleSage technical foundation: Mac Mini #2 set up as production server (security, Tailscale VPN, Docker, monitoring, backups) Self-hosted n8n with Claude API integration 7 production AI agents minimum — lead enrichment, cold email personalisation, reply triage, follow-up sequencer, client reporting, voice agent (Vapi/Retell), plus a 7th you propose after analysing the operational flow with Cy Three landing pages (scalesage.ai/local, /business, /enterprise) using Lovable, v0, or Bolt Tracking infrastructure (GA4, Meta Pixel, Looker Studio dashboards) Integrations ---------- GoHighLevel, Apollo, Instantly, Stripe Documentation + Loom handover The target is the full ScaleSage launch-ready stack in 30 days — Mac Mini server + 7 production agents + 3 landing pages + tracking + integrations + documentation. All of it. Live. Working. Ready for cold email launch on June 2nd. I know it's aggressive — that's intentional. I want to see how you prioritise, ship, and document. A good candidate ships the core spine A strong candidate ships most of it An exceptional candidate ships the whole thing and improves the brief Post-trial — you become a TMC tea ---------- mber at 20-25 hrs/week, working alongside Cy across the portfolio: Belly Full Seasonings brand website + e-commerce Legacy Curriculum educational app builds AI image / video production (Runway, Higgsfield, Flux, Nano Banana Pro, HeyGen avatars) AI voice cloning + persona building (ElevenLabs) AI personalities, content factory, plant/leaf diagnosis tools, lead-gen engines, app prototypes — whatever the portfolio needs Internal tools, dashboards, scaling work for ScaleSage clients You're not on a phased roadmap. You're a TMC tea ---------- mber shipping what the business needs. Variety is the deal. MUST HAVE n8n / Make / Zapier automation experience (n8n self-hosted strongly preferred) Claude / OpenAI API experience — built real workflows, not just played with prompts API / webhook integration — REST, OAuth, rate limits, error handling GHL or similar CRM automation understanding Basic JavaScript or Python for custom logic Landing page builders — Lovable, v0, Bolt, Webflow, Framer, or similar Docker basics or ability to self-host tools on a Mac/Linux server Basic server / security discipline — firewall, VPN (Tailscale), backups, monitoring Loom documentation — you record walkthroughs without being asked Excellent written and spoken English — we work over WhatsApp and Loom. English will be tested live. Self-managing — take a brief and ship, no babysitting AI-native workflow — you use Claude / Cursor / Claude Code daily as power tools Reliable internet, quiet workspace, valid passport NICE TO HAVE Openclaw / claude-flow / agent orchestration tools Supabase / Firebase / Vercel / Cloudflare Stripe payment integration Apollo / Instantly / Clay (cold email infrastructure) AI voice agents — Vapi, Retell, ElevenLabs AI image / video tools — Runway, Higgsfield, Flux, Nano Banana Pro, Sora, Veo, HeyGen, Midjourney App builders — FlutterFlow, Bubble, Replit, Cursor RAG / vector databases — Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector Computer vision APIs (for things like plant/leaf diagnosis or product image analysis) Active GitHub with public commits in the last 90 days Entrepreneurial mindset — you've tried to build something yourself Willingness to travel (Thailand, expenses covered) Openness to relocation long-term if the fit is right You don't need to know every tool already. But you must be the kind of person who can learn a new tool in a weekend, build with it by Monday, and document what you did so the rest of the team can use it. HOW TO APPLY Send a message with: 1. A 5-7 minute Loom walking me through how YOU would tackle the trial-month build. Don't just say hi — show me your brain. Open Loom, share your screen if you want, sketch on a whiteboard, or just talk it through. Cover: How you'd sequence the 30-day build (what you'd do first, second, third) Which tools you'd reach for and why The biggest risk you'd plan for What you'd ship in Week 1 to prove ---------- ntum Any questions or assumptions you'd want me to clarify This Loom is your application. If you can't do this Loom, you can't do the job. No script needed — I want to see how you actually think. 2. Start your written message with the word "AGENT-READY" (so I know you read this carefully) 3. Link to your portfolio + GitHub username 4. One production system you've built — what it does, how you built it, why you built it that way. Screen-share Loom strongly preferred (5 mins, showing it working live, not slideware) 5. Skill self-assessment — for each, mark Strong / Decent / Weak / Never tried: n8n workflows (self-hosted, Docker) Claude / OpenAI API agents GHL / CRM integrations Landing pages with Lovable / v0 / Bolt / Framer Stripe / payment APIs AI voice agents (Vapi / Retell / ElevenLabs) AI image / video workflows (Runway / Flux / HeyGen / Higgsfield) Simple app prototypes (FlutterFlow / Bubble / Cursor) Mac Mini / Linux self-hosting (Docker, Tailscale, security) Documentation + Loom handover Then tell me: which 3 are your strongest? Which 3 are your weakest? How fast could you learn the weak ones? 6. Answer these questions (one or two sentences each): What AI tool do you use most and what do you use it for? What's the most technical thing you've figured out on your own with no one to teach you? What's the most complex production system you've built end-to-end? If you had to automate one part of your own daily life right now, what would it be and how? Describe a problem you solved by writing code or building a workflow without being told how Would you be open to traveling to Thailand for an in-person workshop if needed? (expenses covered) Would you be open to relocating eventually if the fit was right? 7. One paragraph: what's your dream for the next five years? Where do you want to be? What kind of role? What kind of life? 8. Your starting part-time retainer rate ($450-$600/month at 20-25 hrs/week baseline, or your number — explain why) 9. Earliest start date + how many hours/week you can commit 10. One thing you'd push back on or improve in this brief (shows me you think, not just execute) 11. One question you have for me about the role, the company, or me Generic CVs without the above will be ignored. The Loom plan and self-assessment matter more than the CV. If you used AI to help write your application, just tell me which tool — I respect AI use, I don't respect pretending. HIRING PROCESS I review applications + the trial-month plan Loom — Cy and I shortlist together 30-minute video call with shortlist (English tested live, screen-share showing one production system) Selected candidate starts 30-day paid trial — $450 fixed for 20-25 hrs/week End of month, we both d ---------- : continue and grow the role, or part ways clean If continuing ? part-time retainer at $450-$600/month, then path to full-time over time Payment: Wise transfers OR crypto (USDT/USDC on a network of your choice — TRC-20, ERC-20, Base, Solana). Your call. Monthly in arrears, on time, every time. If this sounds like your kind of role — apply. — J W-Blake

title: Video Editor
description: Position: Video Editor (YouTube, Faceless Content) Type: Part-time, remote, project-based Volume: Minimum 12 long-form videos per month Pay: $30 per finished video About Us We produce faceless YouTube content focused on practical, credible education using real-life B-roll footage. No talking heads. No animation. No motion graphics. Just well-paced, professional video that earns trust. What You'll Do - Edit long-form YouTube videos (8-12 minutes) with tight pacing and frequent scene changes - Work from provided scripts to start — training provided to eventually write scripts independently - Create AI-generated voiceover narration from the finished script to begin with. You will later be responsible for creating scripts also, after some instruction. - Source and sync real stock B-roll footage based on scene descriptions - Add lo-fi or cinematic instrumental background music - Deliver YouTube-ready files on deadline - Upload finished videos to YouTube Studio as Private drafts, ready for scheduling - Optimize each video: title, description, tags, chapters, and thumbnail brief What We're Looking For - Intermediate to advanced editor with YouTube experience - Strong English speaking and writing skills are a must - Comfortable with AI voiceover tools and stock footage sourcing - Understands YouTube SEO and optimization basics - Owns your own software subscriptions — we don't provide tools - Delivers clean, finished work without multiple correction rounds Production Standards - Real B-roll only — no animation, no motion graphics, no talking heads - Music fades slightly under narration, swells at transitions - Strong first 45 seconds — hook must land To Apply Send 2-3 examples of faceless YouTube videos you've produced, your preferred tools, and typical turnaround time per video. One more thing: somewhere in this application, a cat is hiding. If you read this far, start your very first line with "The cat found me." Applications that don't begin this way will not be reviewed.

job_title: Content & Communications Writer for Children's E-Commerce Brand
description: JOB OVERVIEW We're a children's e-commerce brand looking for a Content & Communications Writer to help build out our website content, blog, and email/social copy. Right now the priority is finishing a set of doll companion pages — educational, story-driven web pages that teach kids and parents about different cultures. About the Role This is a writing-led execution role, ~20 hrs/week, fully remote. You'll take briefs and follow an approved page template to write warm, informative content for a parent-and-child audience. No design skills needed — you're writing the words, not building the layout. What You'll Do Write companion page content in Shopify: cultural learning sections, "what to say to your child" prompts, holiday guides, activity ideas — following our established page structure Draft blog posts and email/social copy from creative briefs Research any cultural, historical, or product detail you're not already sure of before writing about it Flag anything culturally sensitive for review rather than guessing — final sign-off on cultural content always comes from us Keep ClickUp tasks and timesheets current in real time What We're Looking For Strong, warm English writing for a parent/child audience — this is the core skill Comfortable working from a brief and an existing template without needing to invent structure Some SEO or blog-writing background is a plus Proactive communication — you flag delays and open questions before they become problems Reliable, on-time delivery and invoicing To Apply: Only candidates submitted to this form will be considered ----------

title: Remote Virtual Interviewer & Driver Onboarding Specialist
job_title: Remote Virtual Interviewer & Driver Onboarding Specialist
description: Job Overview We are seeking a highly motivated, organized, and clear-speaking Virtual Interviewer & Driver Onboarding Specialist to join our team. In this role, you will manage our hiring funnel by responding to Indeed advertisements, scheduling applicants, and conducting live virtual interviews. Your main objective is to guide applicants through downloading our mobile app, starting their registration, and explaining how driving with us works. This position requires high-volume communication, meticulous data tracking, and a professional on-camera presence. Key Responsibilities Ad Response & Scheduling: Monitor incoming applications from Indeed, manage the interview schedule, and ensure a steady pipeline of candidates. Virtual Interviews & Onboarding: Conduct live video interviews daily, welcoming and thanking applicants for their time. Explain the role clearly (informing applicants they will operate as independent drivers). Securely guide candidates through the live app download process on their mobile devices. Walk them through initial registration steps (entering Name, Address, Email, Date of Birth, etc.). Provide a clear overview of how the platform operates once the initial registration steps are complete. Metrics & Performance Tracking: Keep meticulous daily logs tracking the exact number of applicants spoken to versus the number of successful app downloads achieved. Quality Assurance: Maintain professional standards at all times, as all video calls and communications are monitored and recorded for quality control. Shift, Schedule, & Compensation Hours: 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM Central Standard Time (CST) Days: Monday through Friday Trial Period: There will be an initial 2-week trial period to evaluate performance, tracking accuracy, and conversion metrics. Location: 100% Remote (Work from home) Required Skills & Qualifications Language Proficiency: Fluent spoken English with a neutral, clear accent for seamless communication with U.S. applicants. Communication: Excellent phone and video communication etiquette; comfortable being on camera all day. Experience: Direct experience making outbound calls or interacting professionally with U.S.-based businesses or individuals. Technical & Workflow Aptitude: Strong organizational skills with the ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment. Comfortable navigating CRM systems, tracking data, and following structured interview scripts. Workspace Requirements: A dedicated, quiet workspace free of background noise, a reliable computer, a high-quality headset, and a rock-solid internet connection. Preferred Experience (A Plus) Cold calling, appointment setting, or lead generation. Customer service, sales support, or Virtual Assistant experience. Prior experience in healthcare outreach or workforce development sectors. Software We Use CRM systems Aircall Gmail Claude AI Application Instructions IMPORTANT: To be considered for this position, you MUST provide the following items with your application: Your current Resume. A short Voice Recording Introduction (link or file). A screenshot of a recent Internet Speed Test. A brief summary of your experience calling U.S. businesses. Explicit confirmation of your availability during 9 AM – 6 PM CST hours. *Please Answer the Following Questions in Your Response*: Describe your experience making outbound calls. Have you worked with U.S. businesses or applicants before? Please elaborate. What specific CRM systems have you used in the past? Are you entirely comfortable speaking with and guiding applicants live on video?

title: Part-Time Etsy App VA – Testing, Research and Content
job_title: Part-Time Etsy App VA – Testing, Research and Content
description: I’m looking for a reliable, thoughtful virtual assistant to help with Cayana, a new web application for Etsy sellers. Knowledge of Etsy Listing Management essential. Cayana helps sellers manage and bulk-edit their Etsy listings in a clearer, more pleasant interface. The first version will launch soon, with more advanced features planned afterward. title: Subscription Retention Consultant — DTC Supplements
description: Type: Full time · Remote · Monday to Friday Salary: $800 – $1,500 USD/month depending on experience, plus a bonus tied to the churn you actually remove. How to apply — read this first Do not send a message here. Do not send a CV here. Go to this link and complete the application: ---------- Pick this role from the list. There is a field inside to upload your CV and link your portfolio — that is where we want them. Applications sent any other way are ignored. What the job is We sell supplements on a subscription. We are good at acquiring customers. We are not good at keeping them, and we know it: a large share of our subscribers write in to cancel before their second charge, and we are losing money we already paid to acquire. That is this job. You own retention. Not the tickets — the numbers behind them. You d ---------- what we say when someone wants to leave, what we offer, when we offer it, and what we change upstream so they stop wanting to leave in the first place. We are hiring for judgment, not for tasks. You have done this at a subscription brand before and you know what works because you watched it work. Your work 1. Find out why they leave, with evidence. Read the cancellation reasons, the support inbox, the refund requests, the chargebacks. Group them. Tell us the three real reasons people churn, ranked by how much money each one costs us. Not opinions — counts. 2. Build the cancellation flow. What we ask, in what order, what we offer against each reason. Pause, skip, change frequency, downsize the order, one-time discount, product swap. You d ---------- the ladder and where the discount sits in it, because a discount given too early is margin we never get back. 3. Fix the money we lose silently. Failed payments and dunning. Card updates. Retry logic. Most subscription brands lose more subscribers to a declined card than to an actual decision to quit, and nobody notices because nobody complains. 4. Work the first 60 days. The subscriber who cancels before charge two never got the product to work. Onboarding emails, dosage expectations, what to feel and when, proactive check-ins. You write the plan and brief whoever executes it. 5. Win them back. Cancelled subscribers are the cheapest customers we will ever have. Build the sequence that brings a share of them back. 6. Report what you changed and what it did. Churn by cohort, retention curve by month, LTV, save rate on cancellation requests, recovered failed payments. Monthly, in numbers, with what you will do next. What we need from you You have run retention for a subscription DTC brand. Not "I did support at a brand that had subscriptions" — you owned the churn number and you were judged on it. You know the tools properly: Recharge, Skio, Bold, Loop or similar, and the email side (Klaviyo or equivalent). You have configured them, not just used them. You can read a cohort. If we hand you six months of subscriber data, you can tell us where the drop happens and what it is worth. You have opinions about save offers, and you can defend them. When to pause instead of discount. When a refund is cheaper than a chargeback. When to let someone go. You write clearly. The emails and flows you design are read by customers, so the words matter. You have seen this before at another brand. We are not the first place where you learn this. Nice to have Supplements, health or wellness specifically. Experience setting up a support function from scratch — helpdesk, macros, refund policy, SOPs. Managing or training support agents. Chargeback dispute experience. Before you apply Some of our brands are in health and women's wellness, including intimacy products. The work is never explicit, but if that topic is not for you, this role is not for you and that is completely fine. What we offer A stable, long-term, full-time position. Real ownership of the number. You d ---------- the offers and the flows. No committee. Direct work with the owner. No middle manager. Paid trial first: we give you our real cancellation reasons and subscriber data for one brand. You come back with the three biggest leaks, what you would build first, and what you expect it to be worth. Good trials get hired within days. Paid on time, every time. Again: the only way to apply is ----------

title: Video Editor / 2D Animator — Long-Form YouTube Anthology (Weekly)
job_title: Video Editor / 2D Animator — Long-Form YouTube Anthology (Weekly)
description: RATE / BUDGET (required field): $2000 USD finished 4 video batch ABOUT THE PROJECT We make long-form anthology videos about history's darkest, strangest corners — think Trust Me Bro, Chat History, Sideprojects. Every 22-minute video contains 12 self-contained stories, each one about 90 seconds, bound by a single premise. The scripts are written, researched, and source-verified. Voiceover is recorded. Your job is everything visual. 2D animation, character-driven, deliberately simple. Thick black outlines, flat fills, expressive faces doing emotional work. Cut-out animation with rigged characters — not frame-by-frame, not photoreal, not AI-generated. Real footage and archival stills carry the history — public-domain photographs, archival film, engravings, museum scans, maps. Roughly half the runtime lives here. The animation integrates with these photos (not pasted on top). Both layers feel like one show. THE FORMAT REQUIREMENTS • 21–23 minute runtime • Hard cuts between items • Visual change every 3–6 seconds (never static) • Comic timing on the deflation beat (dry one-liner after escalation) • Escalation you can see visually (framing, cuts, colour, sound) • Sound design: ambience, SFX, music under the voice, no dead air Each item follows this structure: • Name the thing (bare noun phrase) • Establish the ordinary state • Introduce the deviation • Escalate 2–3 rungs • Deliver the reveal • Dry closing beat (the joke) • Hard cut to next item DELIVERABLES PER VIDEO • Final master: 1080p minimum (4K preferred), 16:9, H.264 • Full sound mix: SFX, ambience, royalty-free music, VO levelled to -14 LUFS • 3 vertical Shorts cuts (45–60s) pulled from strongest items • Source project file + character/asset library • Two revision rounds included per video WHAT YOU NEED MUST HAVE: • After Effects (rigging, cut-out animation, expressions) • Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve • Portfolio: minimum 60+ seconds of long-form animated work (not just shorts/TikToks) • Ability to source, treat, and integrate archival material correctly • Working English to read scripts and understand tone • Reliable weekly turnaround: script + VO delivered Monday ? final cut Thursday NICE TO HAVE: • Illustrator or Procreate for original assets • Experience on faceless/documentary YouTube channels • Understanding of pacing and retention mechanics HOW TO APPLY Send the following in your application message: 1. Link to ONE 60+ second animated piece with timestamp (e.g., "0:30–1:45") — Tell us what you did and why you're proud of it 2. Answer this question (2–3 sentences): "I have 12 items, each 90 seconds, hard cuts between them. Each item escalates then ends with a dry joke. I'm mixing archival photos with 2D animation so they look integrated, not pasted. What's the biggest technical challenge in pulling this off?" 3. Your rate per finished minute + your usual turnaround time for a 22-minute animated piece 4. Include the word "gong farmer" somewhere in your message (This tells us you actually read the job post.) DO NOT APPLY IF: • Your portfolio is only shorts, TikToks, or Reels • You don't have After Effects • You're looking for hourly rates (this is per-video only) • You can't commit to a paid test project first • You need turnarounds longer than 5 days WHY THIS STRUCTURE MATTERS The hard cuts, visual frequency, and deflation beats are the format. Generic editors will add transitions, slow down the pacing, or skip the comic timing. If you don't think in terms of retention, escalation, and deliberate composition, this isn't the fit. TIMELINE • Applications reviewed continuously • Shortlisted candidates: invited to paid test within 2–3 days • Test turnaround: 48 hours • Video 1 starts: week you pass the test

description: We are a growing U.S.-based quilting and fabric company looking for a talented illustrator/artist to help us develop an original collection of artwork for merchandise and other products. This is not a typical Canva or graphic-design position. We are looking for someone who is genuinely talented at illustration and has a strong artistic point of view. Our preferred aesthetic is inspired by vintage American and Scandinavian folk art, block printing, linocut, hand-stamped artwork, vintage textiles and surface-pattern design. We love artwork that feels handmade rather than digitally perfect—stylized florals and botanicals, birds, vines, decorative motifs, expressive hand lettering, simplified shapes, imperfect lines, subtle texture and interesting use of color. Think traditional folk art and block-printed artwork interpreted in a fresh, feminine and modern way. We will provide inspiration images that demonstrate the overall aesthetic we love. These images are for creative direction only. We do not want existing artwork copied, traced or recreated. Our goal is to develop an original and recognizable visual identity for our own brand. Our First Collections Our initial artwork will center around two primary themes: QUILTING, SEWING & MAKING We will create artwork around phrases celebrating quilting, sewing, creativity and handmade things. Examples might include: * “Every Quilt Has a Story” * “Gather the Pieces, Make Something Beautiful” * “There Is Joy in the Making” * “Made by Hand, Made with Heart” FAITH & VINTAGE HYMNS We also plan to develop a collection based on traditional Christian hymns and public-domain hymn lyrics. Examples might include: * “It Is Well with My Soul” * “Amazing Grace, How Sweet the Sound” * “Come Thou Fount of Every Blessing” * “Blessed Assurance” We will provide all phrases and approved hymn lyrics. You will not be responsible for researching copyright. What You’ll Create Initially, designs will primarily be created for apparel, but successful artwork may also be adapted for: * T-shirts and sweatshirts * Tote and project bags * Stickers * Quilt labels * Mugs and other merchandise * Art prints * Packaging and marketing materials * Other products as our collections grow We would love to find an illustrator who can work with us long-term and help establish a cohesive artistic identity across multiple collections. Surface-pattern or textile-design experience is a plus and could lead to additional opportunities in the future. The Style We Love We are especially drawn to: * Folk-art illustration * American and Scandinavian folk-art influences * Block-print and linocut-inspired artwork * Hand-stamped texture * Imperfect, hand-created edges and lines * Vintage textile and surface-pattern influences * Stylized florals, botanicals, leaves, birds and nature * Expressive hand lettering and typography * Decorative and sometimes symmetrical compositions * Warm, interesting and slightly muted color palettes * Artwork that feels collected, handmade and timeless We are NOT looking for: Generic POD/T-shirt graphics, rustic farmhouse signs, Canva-style graphics, corporate vector artwork, stock illustrations, copied artwork or AI-generated designs. You do not need to physically carve blocks or create traditional linocuts. Digital illustration is completely acceptable. We are describing the visual character and handmade quality we want the finished artwork to have. The Person We’re Looking For You may be a great fit if you: * Are an illustrator/artist first, rather than solely a graphic designer * Can draw original botanical, floral and decorative elements * Have a strong understanding of composition * Have excellent typography or hand-lettering instincts * Can interpret a phrase creatively instead of simply placing decorations around text * Understand vintage, folk-art and handmade aesthetics * Can maintain a cohesive style across a collection * Can prepare professional artwork for commercial printing * Communicate well and are comfortable receiving creative feedback * Are interested in ongoing creative work Experience with Procreate, Adobe Illustrator and/or Photoshop is helpful. Artwork Requirements Final deliverables will generally include: * High-resolution 300 DPI artwork * Transparent-background PNG suitable for commercial printing * Print-ready files suitable for DTF/apparel production * Editable/source files when applicable (AI, PSD, Procreate, SVG, etc.) * Additional color versions when requested All commissioned artwork must be original artwork created by you. Approved commissioned artwork will require commercial merchandise usage rights for our company. Specific ownership/usage terms and payment will be agreed upon before commissioned work begins. Paid Trial We plan to select a small number of promising applicants for a paid trial project. Selected artists will receive the same phrase and general creative brief. We intentionally will not tell you exactly what to draw. We want to see how you interpret the concept—your composition, illustration style, typography and artistic instincts. We do not ask applicants to create free sample artwork. The artist who best fits our vision will be offered additional paid projects, with the potential for an ongoing relationship as we develop new collections. How to Apply Please begin your application with the words FOLK ART so we know you have read the entire job description. Then please include: 1. A brief introduction about yourself and your illustration experience. 2. 3–5 examples of your own original artwork that are closest to the aesthetic described above. Please do not send a large generic graphic-design portfolio. 3. Tell us which programs or techniques you use to create your illustrations. 4. Tell us whether you use AI-generated imagery at any point in your illustration process. 5. Tell us about any experience you have with folk art, block-print/linocut styles, hand lettering, surface-pattern design, textiles or apparel artwork. 6. Your desired hourly rate and/or typical price for a completed illustration of this type. 7. Approximately how much time you would expect to spend creating a detailed finished illustration combining hand lettering and botanical/folk-art elements. 8. Tell us why this particular project and aesthetic interest you. Please do not create new artwork or a free sample as part of your application. Portfolio examples are all we need at this stage. We are excited to find an artist whose work we love and hopefully build a long-term creative partnership.

title: Sales & Office Assistant
description: We’re looking for a driven, organized, and confident professional to become a key part of our team and the right-hand person to our General Manager. This is a hands-on role for someone who has strong phone and communication skills, a sales background, excellent organizational abilities, and the ability to take ownership. The primary goal of this position is simple: help take the day-to-day workload off the GM’s plate so they can focus on growing the business. You will play an important role in keeping the office organized, following up with leads and customers, managing tasks through our CRM, tracking important business data, and making sure opportunities don’t fall through the cracks. What You’ll Do Follow up with leads by phone, email, and other communication channels. Make outbound calls and confidently communicate with potential and existing customers. Use our CRM system to track leads, follow-ups, appointments, customer activity, and results. Maintain accurate and up-to-date customer and lead information. Track sales activity, lead activity, follow-up results, and other key business data. Prepare and maintain basic reports and summaries for the GM. Monitor data and identify trends, missed opportunities, and areas that need attention. Help manage the day-to-day operations of the office. Keep the GM organized and assist with administrative and operational tasks. Take ownership of assigned projects and see them through to completion. Monitor open tasks and follow up with team members when needed. Help ensure leads and opportunities are properly followed up with. Schedule appointments and coordinate communication with customers and team members. Identify things that need to be done and take action without always waiting to be asked. Help improve office processes, organization, tracking, and efficiency. Serve as a reliable point person who helps keep the business moving. What We’re Looking For The right person will be proactive, dependable, confident, organized, and comfortable taking ownership. You should have: Strong phone and communication skills. Clear, professional spoken English and the ability to communicate effectively with customers and team members. Previous sales, customer service, or inside sales experience. Confidence speaking with customers and prospects over the phone. Experience working with a CRM or willingness to learn quickly. Strong data entry, tracking, and organizational skills. The ability to accurately track information and maintain clean, reliable data. Strong follow-up skills and attention to detail. The ability to prioritize multiple tasks and stay on top of deadlines. A positive, professional attitude. The ability to work independently and solve problems. A sense of urgency and a willingness to get things done. The Person Who Will Succeed in This Role You’re the type of person who sees something that needs to be done and takes care of it. You don’t need to be told three times to follow up with a customer or update the CRM. You keep your commitments, stay organized, communicate clearly, track the details, and understand that missed calls, missed follow-ups, inaccurate data, and unfinished tasks can cost a business money. Most importantly, you understand that your job is to make the GM’s job easier. As you learn the business, we want you to become someone the GM can trust to handle more and more of the day-to-day responsibilities, allowing them to spend more time focused on sales, strategy, and growing the company. Why This Role Matters This is more than an administrative position. You will have a direct impact on the growth, organization, sales follow-up, and efficiency of the business. If you are someone who enjoys being busy, likes working with people, is comfortable on the phone, pays attention to the numbers, and wants an opportunity to take on more responsibility, this could be a great fit. We’re looking for someone who wants to take ownership, make a difference, and grow with the company.

title: CRO Shopify
description: At Lantern Sol, we’re a dynamic, multicultural team of developers, designers, project managers, and SEO experts dedicated to building exceptional e-commerce websites on Shopify. We’ve helped companies generate over $100 million in e-commerce sales, developed 500+ custom websites and apps, and have been featured speakers on Shopify and Amazon. Shape the future of commerce – Your work will directly impact businesses worldwide. Flexible work environment – Work from anywhere, set your own schedule. Join a thriving global team – Collaborate with top talent across multiple time zones. Professional growth – Stay ahead with continuous learning opportunities and challenging projects. Lantern Sol is looking for a part-time CRO Specialist to support our Shopify and eCommerce clients. This person will provide the deeper CRO expertise behind each account. They will analyze customer and website data, develop testing hypotheses, guide experiment planning, evaluate results, and help communicate the business impact of the work to clients. Each account will still have a Lantern Sol project manager responsible for the overall relationship, timelines, and coordination. Our internal design and development teams will handle execution. The CRO Specialist will own the strategy, analysis, and interpretation that guide the work. What You’ll Do Complete initial CRO audits using data from GA4, Shopify, testing platforms, heatmaps, session recordings, and other available sources. Compare data across platforms to identify conversion issues, customer behavior patterns, and areas of opportunity. Participate in recurring ideation sessions with project managers, designers, and developers. Turn findings and ideas into clear, testable hypotheses. Build and prioritize testing plans based on potential impact, available traffic, confidence, and level of effort. Recommend an appropriate testing cadence for each client rather than applying the same process to every account. Plan tests across different areas of the customer journey, such as the homepage, navigation, product pages, cart, and checkout. Help structure simultaneous tests appropriately so results remain accurate and clients are not exposed to conflicting experiments. Define the audience, success metrics, and measurement approach for each test. Review experiment results and determine whether a hypothesis was confirmed, denied, or requires another iteration. Translate both positive and negative test results into useful insights and clear next steps. Estimate the potential business impact of test results using conversion rate, traffic, average order value, and projected revenue. Update client reporting with results, screenshots, findings, and recommendations. Join client calls when needed to explain testing strategy or present results. Help Lantern Sol improve and document a consistent CRO process that can scale across accounts. Use AI tools to support analysis, ideation, and reporting while applying independent judgment to the final recommendations. You’re a Great Fit If You… Have hands-on experience as a CRO strategist or specialist for Shopify, D2C, or eCommerce brands supporting multiple CRO clients. Experience with Intelligems or similar Shopify experimentation platforms, creating and evaluating A/B or split tests. Understand testing methodology, audience segmentation, sample size, statistical significance, and common factors that can make results unreliable. Can work across GA4, Shopify Analytics, and CRO testing platforms to build a more complete view of performance. Know how to turn data into focused hypotheses and practical testing plans. Can prioritize several testing opportunities without running overlapping experiments that compromise the results. Experience creating or presenting client-facing CRO reports: You know how to frame an unsuccessful experiment as a useful learning rather than simply reporting it as a loss. Can explain data and testing results clearly to clients and team members who may not have a CRO background. Are comfortable collaborating with project managers, designers, and developers without needing to manage the entire account. Are organized, responsive, and able to support multiple accounts in a remote agency environment. Nice to Have Familiarity with Figma and design-to-development workflows. Experience helping an agency build or standardize its CRO delivery process.

title: Grants Coordinator
description: Location: Remote – HQ in Irvine, CA (Pacific Time Zone preferred) Position Type: Part Time - Independent Contractor Hours: 20 hours / 40 hours per week Compensation: $8/hour About Us The Black Girls Mental Health Foundation (BGMHF) is a nonprofit dedicated to eliminating mental health disparities through culturally responsive, trauma-informed care. Our work bridges the gap between perinatal mental health care and racial equity by connecting BIPOC birthing individuals, particularly Black mothers, to high-quality mental health services, trusted providers, and community-rooted support networks. Together with our sister organization, the Black Girls Mental Health Collective, we deliver direct clinical services, train birth and mental health professionals, and advocate for systemic transformation. Our flagship initiative, the BIRTH Network, has supported over 127 families and provided more than 660 hours of culturally affirming therapy to date. With over 30 years of collective experience, our leadership team brings both research expertise and lived experience to the forefront of maternal mental health advocacy. Position Overview The Virtual Assistant (VA) Grant Project Manager keeps Black Girls Mental Health Foundation (BGMHF) on track across the full grant lifecycle; from proposal development through budget tracking, report submission, and program implementation. This role is responsible for monitoring every grant requirement and deadline in ClickUp, sending timely nudges to the staff and program leads responsible for each deliverable, and maintaining a clear, organized view of what's due, what's at risk, and what's complete across all active grants. This is a remote, detail-oriented role suited to someone who is proactive, highly organized, and comfortable holding people accountable to deadlines in a warm, professional way. Primary Responsibilities - Track grant proposal deadlines and requirements in ClickUp, monitoring status from draft through submission. - Monitor grant budget deliverables and timelines, flagging upcoming due dates for financial documentation and spend tracking. - Track grant report submission deadlines (interim, final, and funder-specific reporting requirements) and confirm reports are filed on time. - Monitor program implementation milestones tied to each grant, ensuring activities stay aligned with funder timelines and requirements. - Maintain a master tracker in ClickUp of all active grants, requirements, owners, and due dates across proposals, budgets, reports, and program deliverables. - Send timely nudges and follow-up reminders to team members and program leads on upcoming or overdue grant deliverables. - Flag at-risk deadlines or missing documentation to leadership before they become compliance issues. - Set up new grant projects, tasks, and workflows in ClickUp based on award letters, funder guidelines, and direction from leadership. - Prepare regular grant status updates and progress summaries for leadership review. - Coordinate with the Operations, Finance, and Programs teams to clarify deliverable ownership, timelines, and next steps. - Maintain organized digital records of grant requirements, submission confirmations, and correspondence. - Other duties as assigned. Ideal Candidate Profile Required Qualifications Demonstrated experience with ClickUp (or a comparable project management platform), including task tracking, due dates, and status updates Experience tracking grant requirements, deliverables, or compliance deadlines Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple grants, funders, and deadlines at once Excellent written communication skills, with a professional and friendly tone for deliverable follow-ups Self-starter who can monitor progress and follow up consistently with minimal oversight Comfortable respectfully holding team members and program leads accountable to deadlines Ability to work independently in a remote environment Preferred Qualifications & Skills Experience supporting a nonprofit's grants, programs, or operations Familiarity with common funder requirements (proposal narratives, budget templates, interim/final reporting) Experience working with cross-functional teams (Operations, Finance, Programs) Comfort with basic budget tracking or reading a grant budget line-item Prior virtual assistant or remote administrative support experience Work Environment & Contractor Terms This is a fully remote position. The Accounting Assistant must have a reliable internet connection, a private workspace suitable for handling confidential financial information, and the ability to meet recurring bi-weekly payroll deadlines. CONFIDENTIALITY This role requires access to sensitive financial and personnel information. The Program Manager must maintain strict confidentiality regarding payroll, vendor, and organizational financial matters at all times. How to Apply Please email your resume, brief portfolio (or examples of prior work), and a one-paragraph cover note to ---------- with the subject line: Grants Coordinator Application - [Your Name]. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis through September 2026.

title: Google Ads Expert
description: We're looking for an AI-first Google Ads expert who genuinely loves this work and shows up with the plan. If you light up when you're building a Search or PMax campaign from scratch, use AI as a daily working partner, and prefer driving strategy over taking tasks, we'd love to hear from you. The Role - You'll build and manage multiple Google Ads (and Microsoft Ads) accounts from the ground up, across both ecommerce and lead generation clients. - Most of the work lives in Search and Performance Max, with other campaign types layered in when the account calls for it. - You'll partner with our team to win. We share the wins and we share the work, but you'll lead the thinking on the accounts you own. - Success in your first 30 to 60 days looks like you showing up with the plan. You're telling us what we should be testing, why, and when. You have a clear point of view on what's working across each account, what isn't, and what you want to try next. The bar is strategic ownership. Schedule You'll work part-time hours that fall somewhere between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM EST. We'll set the exact schedule together. There's a real path to full-time as the work grows, so we'd love to know you're open to that conversation down the road. Just want to make sure you can work somewhere inside that window. What We're Looking For - An AI-first mindset. You use AI as a real working partner every day, and it shows in how you work. - Independent problem-solving. You think first, use AI to amplify your thinking, and verify before sending anything off. - A strategy-first approach. You're someone who shows up with the plan and tells us what we should be doing, testing, and improving. You partner with our team on execution, but you lead the thinking on your work. - Deep comfort in Google Ads, GA4, and Search Console. You can navigate them without thinking and read the data without guessing. - Experience running paid search across both ecommerce and lead generation. Both motions are part of the work, so you should be confident in each. - A real love for this work. That comes through fast in conversation, and we'd rather hire someone who has it than someone who's just qualified. How to Apply A few things we'd love you to do, in order. 1. Please start your reply with the word "Jamal." We use this as a small check to spot applicants who read instructions carefully. Without it, we won't be able to review your application. 2. Record a 5-minute video answering the questions below. No script needed. We just want to get a feel for how you think. 3. Share your full tool stack with self-ratings (1 to 10). These ones we already know we need. - Google Ads /10 - GA4 /10 Then add every other tool you use, one per line, with a /10. Include Microsoft Ads if you've used it, AI tools, spreadsheets you've built, niche platforms, the works. Honesty matters more than scoring high. The video will give us a sense of where you actually are. 4. Walk us through your work history. For your last 2 or 3 clients or accounts. - What size was the account when you started (ad spend, revenue, lead volume, whatever metric fits the role)? - What did you do for them? - What was the outcome? Where were they when you started, and where are they now? - If you have current clients, where are those accounts today? We're trying to understand how you measure your own impact. The more specific, the better. 5. Quick confirmation that you can work somewhere inside the hours described above. How You Use AI In your video, spend a minute or so on this. The more specific the better. - Which AI tools you use daily, weekly, and occasionally - A specific example of a task in Google Ads where AI saves you real time, and how you use it - A time AI gave you a wrong or bad output. How you caught it, and what you did about it - Anything you've intentionally chosen NOT to let AI do in your work, and why We're looking for real, lived examples. The specifics tell the story. A Few Questions for Your Video Take these in order, and just talk through them naturally. 1. If you took over a Google Ads account on day one for an ecommerce or lead gen client, walk us through what you'd want to look at in your first week and what your first hypothesis to test would be. 2. Walk us through how you'd diagnose a Search campaign that's spending well but not converting. What do you check, in what order, and why? 3. Tell us about a time you disagreed with a client or stakeholder about how a Google Ads account should be structured. What did you push back on, how did you handle it, and what happened? 4. Why do you love this work? Tell us about a recent campaign or ---------- nt that reminded you why you do it. 5. What's changed about how you structure and signal Google Ads campaigns in the last 12 months (PMax asset groups, search themes, AI Max for Search, broad match plus smart bidding, whatever you've adjusted to)? What's working for you right now and what isn't?

description: I’m looking for an experienced, detail-oriented Video Editor to help me create polished YouTube videos and short-form content for writers. I’m a literary agent and writing educator, and I create practical writing advice for authors. I’m looking for someone who can take professionally recorded footage and turn it into clean, engaging, polished videos for YouTube and TikTok. This is NOT a beginner editing position. I’m looking for someone with a higher level of experience and visual judgment. The biggest thing I need is someone who can see problems without being told about them. For example: • You notice when text is difficult to read against the background and fix it. • You catch awkward cuts, timing issues, or distracting transitions. • You recognize when an on-screen graphic doesn’t look right. • You know how to select complimentary background music and adjust the volume so that the music isn’t competing with me. • You understand when text should appear, disappear, move, or change. • You can make good decisions about pacing without needing every edit specified. • You review your work carefully before sending it to me. • You don’t repeatedly make the same mistake after receiving feedback. • You understand that “technically edited” isn’t the same as “professionally finished.” I want someone who can take ownership of the edit—not someone who waits for me to identify every problem. What you’ll be editing Primarily: • YouTube videos, approximately 8–20 minutes • YouTube Shorts • TikTok videos • Talking-head educational content • Writing/craft education content (online writing classes) • On-screen text, examples, graphics, B-roll, screenshots, music, and occasional visual effects The content is educational rather than entertainment-focused, so clarity, pacing, and professionalism are more important than flashy effects. What I’m looking for You should have: • 3+ years of professional video editing experience (working on someone else’s videos, not your own) • Strong experience editing talking-head YouTube content • Experience creating short-form videos for social media • Excellent sense of pacing and timing • Strong typography and visual-design instincts • Good understanding of text placement, contrast, readability, and composition • Ability to use B-roll and graphics strategically rather than just adding them for the sake of adding them • Excellent attention to detail • Ability to follow a brand/style guide • Ability to work independently • Strong English comprehension • Excellent communication skills • A willingness to take feedback and apply it consistently The most important quality You have good judgment. I don’t want to have to say: “The text is too dark against the background.” I want you to see that before I do. I don’t want to point out the same editing issue three times. I want you to understand the feedback, remember it, and apply it to future videos. You should be the kind of editor who watches the finished video and thinks: “Would I be happy to put my name on this?” Software You should be highly proficient in your primary editing software. Please tell me which software you use and how long you’ve been using it. Experience with CapCut, Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro, After Effects, Canva, or similar tools is a plus. To apply Please include: 1. A link to your portfolio 2. 2–3 examples of YouTube talking-head videos you’ve edited for someone else 3. 2–3 examples of short-form videos you’ve edited for someone else 4. How many years you’ve been professionally editing 5. What editing software you use 6. Your hourly rate 7. Your typical turnaround time for a 10–15 minute YouTube video 8. Your availability and approximate number of hours you can work per week 9. A brief explanation of how you make sure you catch visual or editing problems before delivering a video Please do not send a generic application. Tell me specifically about your experience editing talking-head educational content and what you do to ensure a finished video is polished and professional. I’m looking for a long-term editor who can become familiar with my content, style, and expectations and eventually require very little hand-holding. If you were stranded on an island and could only have three things, what would they be? If you’re highly experienced, detail-oriented, visually aware, and take pride in catching the little things, I’d love to see your work.

title: cold outreach / client acquisition
description: I’m looking for someone to help me build and eventually run our outbound outreach. Right now we’re mainly targeting insurance agents and home service companies — roofing, gutters, garage doors, pest control, concrete, remodeling, and similar businesses. The basic job is straightforward. Find the right companies and people, find their contact information, get everything into our CRM, and reach out through email and SMS to start conversations about our lead generation services. But I’m not really looking for someone who just wants me to hand them a list of tasks every morning. I want someone who can learn what we’re doing, understand what works, and eventually take ownership of the entire process. In the beginning I’ll be heavily involved. I’ll help build the process, write the messaging, d ---------- who we’re targeting, set up the tools, etc. From there, I want you to start taking more and more of it off my plate. If one message is getting twice as many responses as another, I want you to notice it. If a certain type of contractor is responding better, I want you to notice it. If our data sucks, follow-ups aren’t happening, or something is falling through the cracks, I want you to catch it. I’m VERY focused on organization and numbers. I don’t care that we sent 10,000 messages. I care what happened because we sent them. How many people did we contact? How many responded? How many were interested? How many appointments did we set? How many showed up? How many became customers? That’s how I want us thinking about this. Your day-to-day will include finding prospects, researching contact information, keeping the CRM organized, sending email and SMS outreach, handling replies, following up, and getting interested people onto calls. Your English needs to be fluent and conversational. You don’t need to be some amazing salesperson. But you do need basic sales ability and enough common sense to have a normal conversation with a business owner without sounding like you’re reading from a script. I’ll provide and pay for all of the software, CRM, data tools, email/SMS tools, AI tools, and anything else we need. We’ll use Slack for communication. There’s a lot of room to grow here. If you’re good, I don’t want you doing data entry forever. I want you eventually running the process, helping improve it, and potentially managing other people as we scale it. I have multiple businesses and generate a lot of leads, so this is something I plan on building pretty aggressively. I’m ready to hire immediately. When you apply, tell me about any outreach or lead generation you’ve done, what CRMs and outreach tools you’ve used, whether you’ve worked with US businesses, and most importantly, give me an example of something you were responsible for where you improved the process instead of just doing what you were told. Also tell me your availability and expected monthly salary. Start your application with the word “OWNER” so I know you actually read this.

Applicants must understand that unauthorized lead sharing is a serious breach of trust and company policy. Confirmed violations may result in immediate termination and may be reported to OnlineJobs.ph in accordance with the platform’s policies. Briefly describe your previous Amazon Online Arbitrage sourcing experience. 3. List the sourcing strategies you have personally used.
